children.title: Classical Hessian Models
children.top_down_role: Twice-smooth specialization and its local curvature representation.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is twice Fréchet differentiable at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The local second-order model is the quadratic form \(w\mapsto\langle w,\nabla^2f(\bar x)w\rangle\).

notation.meaning: gradient of f at the reference point
Hessian of f at the reference point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional twice-smooth Taylor model with the standard one-half normalization.

source_refs.source_title: Modern Nonconvex Nondifferentiable Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(w\in\mathbb{R}^n\), twice Fréchet differentiability gives
\[
f(\bar x+t w)=f(\bar x)+t\langle\nabla f(\bar x),w\rangle+\tfrac12t^2\langle w,\nabla^2f(\bar x)w\rangle+o(t^2)
\]
as \(t\to0\). Consequently,
\[
\lim_{t\to0}\frac{2\bigl(f(\bar x+t w)-f(\bar x)-t\langle\nabla f(\bar x),w\rangle\bigr)}{t^2}=\langle w,\nabla^2f(\bar x)w\rangle.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a twice-smooth function, the Hessian quadratic form is exactly the second-order term in the local Taylor expansion.
knowledge_statements.title: Classical Hessian Models

children.title: Second-Order Directional Derivatives
children.top_down_role: Directional second-order models beyond twice-smooth functions.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\), \(f(\bar x)\in\mathbb{R}\), and the directional derivative \(df(\bar x)(w)\) exists finitely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When the displayed limit exists, it defines the second-order directional derivative \(d^2f(\bar x)(w)\).

notation.meaning: second-order directional derivative in direction w

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided second-order directional derivative along a fixed ray.

source_refs.source_title: Modern Nonconvex Nondifferentiable Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The second-order directional derivative of \(f\) at \(\bar x\) in direction \(w\) is
\[
d^2f(\bar x)(w):=\lim_{t\downarrow0}\frac{f(\bar x+t w)-f(\bar x)-t\,df(\bar x)(w)}{\tfrac12t^2},
\]
provided this extended-real limit exists. The lower second-order directional derivative is obtained by replacing the limit with \(\liminf_{t\downarrow0}\); it remains meaningful when the ordinary limit fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This derivative measures the residual quadratic growth along one fixed direction after subtracting the first-order directional term.
knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Directional Derivatives

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-order directional derivatives and twice semidifferentiability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions and basic identities for second-order directional and subderivative models of a real-valued semidifferentiable function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathcal O\to\mathbb R\), where \(\mathcal O\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is open, and suppose \(f\) is semidifferentiable at \(\bar x\in\mathcal O\). When the limit exists, define \(\frac12 f^{(2)}(\bar x;v)=\lim_{\tau\downarrow0}\frac{f(\bar x+\tau v)-f(\bar x)-\tau f'(\bar x;v)}{\tau^2}\). For \(v,w\in\mathbb R^n\), define \(\frac12\mathrm d^2f(\bar x\mid v)(w)=\liminf_{w'\to w,\,\tau\downarrow0}\frac{f(\bar x+\tau w')-f(\bar x)-\tau v^\top w'}{\tau^2}\), and define \(\frac12\mathrm d^2f(\bar x)(w)=\liminf_{w'\to w,\,\tau\downarrow0}\frac{f(\bar x+\tau w')-f(\bar x)-\tau\mathrm df(\bar x)(w')}{\tau^2}\). The functions \(f^{(2)}(\bar x;\cdot)\) and \(\mathrm d^2f(\bar x\mid v)(\cdot)\) are positively homogeneous of degree two. The function is twice directionally differentiable at \(\bar x\) when it is directionally differentiable there and \(f^{(2)}(\bar x;v)\) exists for every \(v\). It is twice semidifferentiable at \(\bar x\) when it is semidifferentiable there and the defining limit for \(\mathrm d^2f(\bar x)(w)\) exists for every \(w\). In the latter case, \(\mathrm d^2f(\bar x)(w)=f^{(2)}(\bar x;w)\) for every \(w\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The second-order directional derivative removes the first directional term from a directional difference quotient. The second-order subderivatives use lower limits under simultaneous perturbation of the direction. These objects are positively homogeneous of degree two. Twice directional differentiability requires all fixed-direction limits, whereas twice semidifferentiability requires the perturbed-direction limits. Under twice semidifferentiability, the unparameterized second-order subderivative equals the second-order directional derivative in every direction.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal O\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is open}
\bar x\in\mathcal O
f:\mathcal O\to\mathbb R\text{ is semidifferentiable at }\bar x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is twice semidifferentiable at }\bar x\implies \mathrm d^2f(\bar x)(w)=f^{(2)}(\bar x;w)\quad\forall w\in\mathbb R^n.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Continuity of the second derivative under twice semidifferentiability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality and continuity of directional second-order models under twice semidifferentiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f\) is twice semidifferentiable at \(\bar x\) in an open set \(\mathcal O\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), then \(\mathrm d^2f(\bar x)(\cdot)=f^{(2)}(\bar x;\cdot)\), and this common function is continuous on \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a function twice semidifferentiable at the reference point, its second-order subderivative and second-order directional derivative coincide, and their common function of the direction is continuous on the whole space.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal O\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is open}
\bar x\in\mathcal O
f\text{ is twice semidifferentiable at }\bar x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm d^2f(\bar x)(\cdot)=f^{(2)}(\bar x;\cdot)\in C(\mathbb R^n).

children.top_down_role: Extended-real second-order directional models relative to first-order covectors.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Variational Analysis

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is proper and \(f(\bar x)\in\mathbb{R}\).
\(\bar v\in\mathbb{R}^n\) is a chosen first-order covector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting extended-real function \(d^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v):\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is the second subderivative relative to \(\bar v\).

notation.meaning: second-order difference quotient relative to the covector

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard finite-dimensional second-subderivative definition with one-half normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rockafellar–Wets lower epigraphical second-order quotient convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(t>0\), set
\[
\Delta_t^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w):=\frac{f(\bar x+t w)-f(\bar x)-t\langle\bar v,w\rangle}{\tfrac12t^2}.
\]
The second subderivative of \(f\) at \(\bar x\) relative to \(\bar v\) is
\[
d^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w):=\liminf_{\substack{t\downarrow0\\w'\to w}}\Delta_t^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w').
\]
The perturbation \(w'\to w\) distinguishes this lower epigraphical object from a fixed-ray second-order directional derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The second subderivative is the lower epigraphical limit of quadratic difference quotients after subtracting a specified covector’s linear term.
knowledge_statements.title: Second Subderivatives

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formula is a standard second-subderivative convention, but no inspectable source establishes the normalization and joint liminf convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structural and domain properties of second subderivatives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower semicontinuity, degree-two homogeneity, covector dependence, infinite-value cases, and properness restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}} satisfy f(\bar x)<\infty. The functions d^2f(\bar x) and d^2f(\bar x\mid v) are lower semicontinuous and positively homogeneous of degree 2. For fixed w, d^2f(\bar x\mid v)(w) depends concavely on v, and\[
d^2f(\bar x\mid v)(w)=+\infty\quad\text{if }\langle v,w\rangle<df(\bar x)(w),
\]\[
d^2f(\bar x\mid v)(w)=-\infty\quad\text{if }\langle v,w\rangle>df(\bar x)(w).
\]Thus a finite value requires \langle v,w\rangle=df(\bar x)(w), while\[
\operatorname{dom}d^2f(\bar x\mid v)\subset\{w:df(\bar x)(w)\leq\langle v,w\rangle\}.
\]If d^2f(\bar x\mid v) is proper, then\[
v\in\widehat\partial f(\bar x),\qquad
\operatorname{dom}d^2f(\bar x\mid v)\subset\{w:df(\bar x)(w)=\langle v,w\rangle\}\subset N_{\widehat\partial f(\bar x)}(v).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Second subderivatives are lower semicontinuous and positively homogeneous of degree two. For a fixed direction, the covector-relative value is concave in the covector. Strict mismatch between the directional derivative and covector pairing forces positive or negative infinity. Properness requires a regular subgradient and restricts the domain to equality directions lying in the normal cone to the regular subdifferential.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}
f(\bar x)<\infty
v,w\in\mathbb{R}^n
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d^2f(\bar x),d^2f(\bar x\mid v)\text{ are lsc and degree-2 positively homogeneous};\quad d^2f(\bar x\mid v)\text{ proper}\Rightarrow v\in\widehat\partial f(\bar x),\ \operatorname{dom}d^2f(\bar x\mid v)\subset\{w:df(\bar x)(w)=\langle v,w\rangle\}\subset N_{\widehat\partial f(\bar x)}(v).

children.title: Second Epi-Derivatives
children.top_down_role: Second-order epigraphical limit objects.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is proper, \(f(\bar x)\in\mathbb{R}\), and \(\bar v\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The second epi-derivative, when defined, is the epigraphical limit of \(\Delta_t^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)\).

notation.meaning: quadratic difference quotient relative to the covector

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard sequential definition of a second epi-derivative
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential finite-dimensional epigraphical limit as the scale tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(q_t:=\Delta_t^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)\) for \(t>0\). A function \(q:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is the second epi-derivative of \(f\) at \(\bar x\) relative to \(\bar v\) when
\[
q=\operatorname*{e-lim}_{t\downarrow0}q_t.
\]
Equivalently, for every \(w\), every sequences \(t_k\downarrow0\) and \(w_k\to w\) satisfy \(q(w)\le\liminf_k q_{t_k}(w_k)\), and for every sequence \(t_k\downarrow0\) there exist \(w_k\to w\) with \(q(w)\ge\limsup_k q_{t_k}(w_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A second epi-derivative is the epigraphical limit of the entire family of second-order difference-quotient functions.
knowledge_statements.title: Second Epi-Derivatives

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sequential epi-limit formulation is plausible, but its exact quantifiers and identification as the second epi-derivative require an authoritative locator.

children.title: Twice Epi-Differentiability
children.top_down_role: Existence and convergence regime for second epi-derivatives.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is proper, \(f(\bar x)\in\mathbb{R}\), and \(\bar v\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under the stated convergence and properness conditions, \(f\) is twice epi-differentiable at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\).

notation.meaning: quadratic difference quotient relative to the covector

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard proper epi-limit criterion for twice epi-differentiability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proper twice epi-differentiability relative to a fixed first-order covector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The function \(f\) is twice epi-differentiable at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\) if the family \(\Delta_t^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)\) epi-converges as \(t\downarrow0\) to a proper extended-real function. In that case,
\[
\operatorname*{e-lim}_{t\downarrow0}\Delta_t^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)=d^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v),
\]
where the equality follows because the epigraphical lower limit is the second subderivative. Properness excludes a limit identically equal to \(+\infty\) or taking the value \(-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Twice epi-differentiability means that quadratic difference quotients epi-converge to a proper second-order model.
knowledge_statements.title: Twice Epi-Differentiability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A source is required to confirm whether properness belongs to twice epi-differentiability itself or to the stronger notion of proper twice epi-differentiability.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Proper Twice Epi-Differentiability from Full Amenability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives a neighborhood-uniform sufficient condition for proper twice epi-differentiability at every nearby domain point and subgradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is fully amenable at \(\bar x\), then there exists \(V\in\mathcal N(\bar x)\) such that, for every \(x\in V\cap\operatorname{dom}f\) and every \(v\in\partial f(x)\), \(f\) is properly twice epi-differentiable at \(x\) for \(v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full amenability at x-bar guarantees a neighborhood in which the function is properly twice epi-differentiable at every domain point for every subgradient there.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}
f\text{ is fully amenable at }\bar x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists V\in\mathcal N(\bar x)\ \forall x\in V\cap\operatorname{dom}f\ \forall v\in\partial f(x):\ f\text{ is properly twice epi-differentiable at }x\text{ for }v.

children.title: Parabolic Subderivatives
children.top_down_role: Function models using first- and second-order directional scaling.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\), \(f(\bar x)\in\mathbb{R}\), and \(df(\bar x)(w)\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The value \(d^2f(\bar x)(w\mid z)\) measures second-order growth along arcs with velocity \(w\) and acceleration \(z\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard lower parabolic difference-quotient definition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower parabolic derivative using velocity and acceleration variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a direction \(w\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and a second-order correction \(z\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the parabolic subderivative is
\[
d^2f(\bar x)(w\mid z):=\liminf_{\substack{t\downarrow0\\z'\to z}}\frac{f(\bar x+t w+\tfrac12t^2z')-f(\bar x)-t\,df(\bar x)(w)}{\tfrac12t^2}.
\]
It is an extended-real function of \(z\) for each fixed first-order direction \(w\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The parabolic subderivative records quadratic growth along perturbed arcs having prescribed first-order velocity and second-order acceleration.
knowledge_statements.title: Parabolic Subderivatives

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The velocity-acceleration formula is standard-looking, but the normalization, perturbation convention, and terminology need an exact source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lower semicontinuity and comparison inequality for parabolic subderivatives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relates the parabolic subderivative to the second subderivative relative to a vector satisfying the directional equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\), with \(f(\bar x)\) and \(df(\bar x)(w)\) finite. Then \(z\mapsto d^2f(\bar x)(w\mid z)\) is lower semicontinuous. For every \(v\) satisfying \(df(\bar x)(w)=\langle v,w\rangle\),
\[
\inf_z\{d^2f(\bar x)(w\mid z)-\langle v,z\rangle\}\ge d^2f(\bar x\mid v)(w).
\]
The left side equals the lower limit of \(\Delta_\tau^2f(\bar x\mid v)(w')\) as \(\tau\searrow0\) and \(w'\to w\), restricted by boundedness of \((w'-w)/\tau\); the right side is the corresponding lower limit without this restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The parabolic subderivative is lower semicontinuous in its second-order direction. For a vector v satisfying the stated first-order directional equality, subtracting its linear term and minimizing gives an upper bound on the relative second subderivative. The left side restricts recovery directions to approach w at order τ, whereas the right side has no such rate restriction.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}
f(\bar x)<\infty
df(\bar x)(w)<\infty
df(\bar x)(w)=\langle v,w\rangle
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z\mapsto d^2f(\bar x)(w\mid z)\text{ is lsc},\qquad \inf_z\{d^2f(\bar x)(w\mid z)-\langle v,z\rangle\}\ge d^2f(\bar x\mid v)(w)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Parabolic calculus for fully amenable functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Establishes parabolic epi-differentiability, regularity, conjugacy, and a composite formula for fully amenable functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) be fully amenable at \(\bar x\). Then \(f\) is parabolically epi-differentiable at \(\bar x\) for every \(w\in\operatorname{dom}df(\bar x)\) and parabolically regular at \(\bar x\) for every \(v\in\partial f(\bar x)\). For each such \(w\), the function \(z\mapsto d^2f(\bar x)(w\mid z)\) is lower semicontinuous, proper, convex, and piecewise linear, and is conjugate to
\[
v\mapsto\begin{cases}-d^2f(\bar x\mid v)(w),&v\in\partial f(\bar x\mid w),\\+\infty,&v\notin\partial f(\bar x\mid w),\end{cases}
\]
where
\[
\partial f(\bar x\mid w):=\operatorname*{argmax}_{v\in\partial f(\bar x)}\langle v,w\rangle.
\]
For any local full-amenability representation \(f=g\circ F\), with \(g\) piecewise linear-quadratic,
\[
d^2f(\bar x)(w\mid z)=d^2g(F(\bar x))\bigl(\nabla F(\bar x)w\mid\nabla^2F(\bar x)[w,w]+\nabla F(\bar x)z\bigr)
\]
and
\[
d^2f(\bar x)(w\mid z)=d^2g(F(\bar x))(\nabla F(\bar x)w)+\max_{y\in Y(\bar x\mid w)}\left\langle y,\nabla^2F(\bar x)[w,w]+\nabla F(\bar x)z\right\rangle,
\]
where
\[
Y(\bar x\mid w):=\operatorname*{argmax}_{y\in\partial g(F(\bar x))}\langle y,\nabla F(\bar x)w\rangle.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full amenability implies parabolic epi-differentiability in every direction with finite first subderivative and parabolic regularity for every subgradient. The parabolic subderivative is a proper lower-semicontinuous convex piecewise-linear function of the second-order direction, has the stated conjugate representation, and satisfies an explicit composite formula for a smooth mapping followed by a piecewise linear-quadratic function.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\text{ is fully amenable at }\bar x
w\in\operatorname{dom}df(\bar x)
f=g\circ F\text{ locally with }g\text{ piecewise linear-quadratic, for the composite formula}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is parabolically epi-differentiable for every }w\in\operatorname{dom}df(\bar x)\text{ and parabolically regular for every }v\in\partial f(\bar x),\text{ with the stated conjugacy and composite formula.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Parabolic subderivative and parabolic epi-differentiability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines second-order parabolic growth and epigraphical convergence along a fixed first-order direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\), with \(f(\bar x)\) and \(df(\bar x)(w)\) finite. For \(z\in\mathbb{R}^n\),
\[
d^2f(\bar x)(w\mid z):=\liminf_{\substack{\tau\searrow0\\z'\to z}}\frac{f(\bar x+\tau w+\tfrac12\tau^2z')-f(\bar x)-\tau df(\bar x)(w)}{\tfrac12\tau^2}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
d^2f(\bar x)(w\mid\cdot)=\operatorname{e-liminf}_{\tau\searrow0}\Delta_\tau^2f(\bar x)(w\mid\cdot).
\]
The function \(f\) is parabolically epi-differentiable at \(\bar x\) for \(w\) if this epigraphical lower limit is the epigraphical limit and is not identically \(+\infty\). Equivalently, for every \(z\) there exist \(z_\tau\to z\) such that \(\Delta_\tau^2f(\bar x)(w\mid z_\tau)\to d^2f(\bar x)(w\mid z)\); this can also be expressed using an arc \(\xi\) with \(\xi(0)=\bar x\), \(\xi'_+(0)=w\), \(\xi''_+(0)=z\), and \((f\circ\xi)''_+(0)=d^2f(\bar x)(w\mid z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The parabolic subderivative is the lower limit of normalized second-order differences along perturbations of the form x̄+τw+(τ²/2)z′. Parabolic epi-differentiability means that these quotient functions epigraphically converge to a function not identically positive infinity, with recovery perturbations—or equivalently suitable arcs—for every second-order direction.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}
f(\bar x)<\infty
df(\bar x)(w)<\infty
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d^2f(\bar x)(w\mid z)=\liminf_{\substack{\tau\searrow0\\z'\to z}}\frac{f(\bar x+\tau w+\tfrac12\tau^2z')-f(\bar x)-\tau df(\bar x)(w)}{\tfrac12\tau^2}

notation.meaning: second subderivative relative to the covector

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-form parabolic regularity on directions critical for the chosen covector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The function \(f\) is parabolically regular at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\) in the value-form sense if, for every \(w\) with \(df(\bar x)(w)=\langle\bar v,w\rangle\),
\[
d^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)=\inf_{z\in\mathbb{R}^n}\bigl\{d^2f(\bar x)(w\mid z)-\langle\bar v,z\rangle\bigr\},
\]
with the convention that the infimum is \(+\infty\) when every term is \(+\infty\). This condition makes the epigraphical second-order model recoverable from parabolic accelerations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parabolic regularity says the second subderivative equals the best parabolic acceleration model after subtracting the covector pairing.
knowledge_statements.title: Parabolic Regularity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed value identity may be a consequence of a sequence-based parabolic-regularity condition rather than its definition. Exact hypotheses and the intended variant require a source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Parabolic regularity of a function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines equality in the comparison between parabolic and relative second subderivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is parabolically regular at \(\bar x\) for \(v\) if \(f(\bar x)<\infty\) and, for every \(w\) satisfying \(df(\bar x)(w)=\langle v,w\rangle\),
\[
\inf_z\{d^2f(\bar x)(w\mid z)-\langle v,z\rangle\}=d^2f(\bar x\mid v)(w).
\]
Equivalently, whenever such a \(w\) has \(d^2f(\bar x\mid v)(w)<\infty\), there exist \(\tau^\nu\searrow0\) and \(w^\nu\to w\) such that
\[
\Delta_{\tau^\nu}^2f(\bar x\mid v)(w^\nu)\to d^2f(\bar x\mid v)(w),\qquad
\limsup_\nu\frac{\lVert w^\nu-w\rVert}{\tau^\nu}<\infty.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parabolic regularity at x̄ for v means that the comparison inequality between parabolic and relative second subderivatives is an equality for every direction satisfying the first-order directional equality. Equivalently, every finite relative second-subderivative value in such a direction has a recovery sequence approaching the direction at order τ.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}
f(\bar x)<\infty
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall w\text{ with }df(\bar x)(w)=\langle v,w\rangle:\quad \inf_z\{d^2f(\bar x)(w\mid z)-\langle v,z\rangle\}=d^2f(\bar x\mid v)(w)

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The outer second-order tangent set to \(C\) at \(\bar x\) in direction \(w\) is
\[
T_C^2(\bar x,w):=\operatorname*{Limsup}_{t\downarrow0}\frac{C-\bar x-tw}{\tfrac12t^2}.
\]
Equivalently, \(z\in T_C^2(\bar x,w)\) precisely when there exist sequences \(t_k\downarrow0\) and \(z_k\to z\) such that
\[
\bar x+t_k w+\tfrac12t_k^2z_k\in C
\]
for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outer second-order tangents are acceleration limits realized along at least one sequence of feasible parabolic arcs.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is closed, \(\bar x\in C\), and \(w\in T_C(\bar x)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The set \(C\) is parabolically derivable at \(\bar x\) in direction \(w\) if
\[
T_C^{i,2}(\bar x,w)=T_C^2(\bar x,w).
\]
Thus every acceleration obtainable along some vanishing sequence is obtainable, up to convergent acceleration perturbations, along every vanishing sequence. If this equality holds for every \(w\in T_C(\bar x)\), then \(C\) is parabolically derivable at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parabolic derivability means the inner and outer second-order tangent sets coincide, eliminating dependence on the chosen step-size sequence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Parabolic geometry of fully amenable sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Describes parabolic derivability and regularity of fully amenable sets and represents their second-order tangent sets through indicator-function second subderivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fully amenable set is parabolically derivable in every tangent direction and parabolically regular for every normal vector. Its second-order tangent set in each tangent direction is nonempty and polyhedral. Its support function equals the negative second subderivative of the indicator for normal vectors orthogonal to the direction and is positive infinity otherwise.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall w\in T_C(\bar x):\ T_C^2(\bar x\mid w)\ne\varnothing\text{ is polyhedral and }\sigma_{T_C^2(\bar x\mid w)}(v)=\begin{cases}-d^2\delta_C(\bar x\mid v)(w),&v\in N_C(\bar x),\ v\perp w,\\+\infty,&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-Order Tangent Sets and Parabolic Derivability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines directional second-order tangent geometry, feasible-arc realization, and its failure boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\bar x\in C\subset\mathbb R^n\) and \(w\in T_C(\bar x)\), define \[T_C^2(\bar x\mid w):=\limsup_{\tau\searrow0}\frac{C-\bar x-\tau w}{\tfrac12\tau^2}.\] The set \(C\) is parabolically derivable at \(\bar x\) for \(w\) if this outer limit is nonempty and is attained as a full limit; equivalently, every \(z\in T_C^2(\bar x\mid w)\) is realized by an arc \(\xi:[0,\varepsilon]\to C\) satisfying \(\xi(0)=\bar x\), \(\xi'_+(0)=w\), and \(\xi''_+(0)=z\). Without parabolic derivability, an element of the outer limit may be obtainable only along sequences. The set \(T_C^2(\bar x\mid w)\) need not be a cone and may be empty. For \(C=\{(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb R^2:x_1^4-x_2^3=0\}\), \(\bar x=(0,0)\), and \(w=(1,0)\), it is empty, so \(C\) is not parabolically derivable in that direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The second-order tangent set contains limiting quadratic corrections to motion in a tangent direction. Parabolic derivability requires every such correction to be realized by a feasible arc rather than only by selected sequences. The set can be empty and need not be a cone.
assumptions_latex: C\subset\mathbb R^n
\bar x\in C
w\in T_C(\bar x)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_C^2(\bar x\mid w)=\limsup_{\tau\searrow0}\frac{C-\bar x-\tau w}{\tfrac12\tau^2};\quad C\text{ is parabolically derivable exactly under the stated nonempty full-limit and arc-realization condition.}

children.title: Primal Curvature Representations
children.top_down_role: Second-order curvature information expressed through feasible-set displacement geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is closed, \(\bar x\in C\), \(\bar v\in N_C(\bar x)\), and \(w\in K_C(\bar x,\bar v)\).
\(C\) is parabolically derivable and parabolically regular at \(\bar x\) in direction \(w\) relative to \(\bar v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The curvature value is the negative support function \(-\sigma_{T_C^2(\bar x,w)}(\bar v)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Indicator-function curvature represented through feasible parabolic accelerations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the stated derivability and regularity hypotheses, the second subderivative of the indicator function has the primal representation
\[
d^2\delta_C(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)=\inf_{z\in T_C^2(\bar x,w)}\{-\langle\bar v,z\rangle\}=-\sigma_{T_C^2(\bar x,w)}(\bar v).
\]
The infimum over the empty set is \(+\infty\). Thus the covector-relative curvature of \(C\) in the critical direction \(w\) is determined by the support of its feasible second-order accelerations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under parabolic regularity, indicator curvature equals the negative support of the second-order tangent set in the normal direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Curvature Representations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The support-function identity is algebraically consistent, but the exact derivability, regularity, and normal-cone hypotheses under which it represents the indicator's second subderivative require an authoritative source.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each direction \(w\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the second-order normal geometry of \(C\) at \((\bar x,\bar v)\) is represented by the graphical derivative of its limiting normal mapping:
\[
DN_C(\bar x,\bar v)(w):=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^n\mid (w,z)\in T_{\operatorname{gph}N_C}(\bar x,\bar v)\}.
\]
Thus \(z\in DN_C(\bar x,\bar v)(w)\) precisely when there exist \(t_k\downarrow0\) and \((w_k,z_k)\to(w,z)\) such that \((\bar x+t_kw_k,\bar v+t_kz_k)\in\operatorname{gph}N_C\) for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Second-order normal geometry records all first-order variations of a normal vector accompanying a prescribed first-order displacement of the base point.

children.title: Primal–Dual Curvature Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Regimes connecting primal curvature descriptions with dual normal constructions.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(\bar v\in N_C(\bar x)\), and \(\delta_C\) is twice epi-differentiable at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(DN_C(\bar x,\bar v)(w)=\partial\!\left(\tfrac12 d_e^2\delta_C(\bar x\mid\bar v)\right)(w)\) for every \(w\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex twice-epi-differentiable form of the primal–dual correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the second epi-derivative by
\[
d_e^2\delta_C(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w):=\operatorname*{e\!\!-\!lim}_{t\downarrow0}\frac{\delta_C(\bar x+tw)-\delta_C(\bar x)-t\langle\bar v,w\rangle}{\tfrac12t^2}.
\]
Then the proto-derivative of the normal mapping, which equals its graphical derivative under the stated hypothesis, satisfies
\[
DN_C(\bar x,\bar v)(w)=\partial\!\left(\tfrac12d_e^2\delta_C(\bar x\mid\bar v)\right)(w)
\quad\text{for every }w\in\mathbb{R}^n.
\]
Hence primal second-order epigraphical curvature determines the dual variation of normals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex twice-epi-differentiable set indicator, the derivative of the normal mapping equals the subdifferential of one-half its second epi-derivative.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Curvature Correspondence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The duality content kind and finite-dimensional convex scope fit the terminal container, and the displayed correspondence is plausible under the stated normalization. However, no citation is supplied, and the precise factor, twice-epi-differentiability hypothesis, proto-derivative conclusion, and equality with the graphical derivative require an authoritative theorem locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The graphical derivative of \(F\) at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) is the positively homogeneous multifunction \(DF(\bar x,\bar y):\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^m\) defined by
\[
DF(\bar x,\bar y)(u):=\{v\in\mathbb{R}^m\mid (u,v)\in T_{\operatorname{gph}F}(\bar x,\bar y)\}.
\]
Equivalently, \(v\in DF(\bar x,\bar y)(u)\) when some \(t_k\downarrow0\) and \((u_k,v_k)\to(u,v)\) satisfy \(\bar y+t_kv_k\in F(\bar x+t_ku_k)\) for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The graphical derivative consists of output velocities attainable along graph points having the prescribed input velocity.

children.title: Strict Graphical Derivatives
children.top_down_role: Strict graph-variation models for uniform local behavior.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^m\) and \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_*F(\bar x,\bar y)(u)=\{v:(u,v)\in T^P_{\operatorname{gph}F}(\bar x,\bar y)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the paratingent-cone convention for the strict graphical derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The strict graphical derivative of \(F\) at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) is defined through the paratingent cone by
\[
D_*F(\bar x,\bar y)(u):=\{v\in\mathbb{R}^m\mid (u,v)\in T^P_{\operatorname{gph}F}(\bar x,\bar y)\}.
\]
Thus \(v\in D_*F(\bar x,\bar y)(u)\) exactly when there exist graph points \((x_k,y_k)\to(\bar x,\bar y)\), numbers \(t_k\downarrow0\), and \((u_k,v_k)\to(u,v)\) such that \((x_k+t_ku_k,y_k+t_kv_k)\in\operatorname{gph}F\) for all \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The strict graphical derivative permits difference quotients based at arbitrary nearby graph points, capturing uniform local graph variation.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Graphical Derivatives

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The paratingent-cone definition and nearby-base-point characterization are internally consistent and fit the strict graphical derivative container. Because notation and terminology for strict graphical derivatives vary across sources, an authoritative source with an exact definition or theorem locator is required before accepting this convention.

The limiting coderivative of \(F\) at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) is the multifunction \(D^*F(\bar x,\bar y):\mathbb{R}^m\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^n\) given by

D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*):=\{x^*\in\mathbb{R}^n\mid (x^*,-y^*)\in N_{\operatorname{gph}F}(\bar x,\bar y)\}.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^m\) and \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is proto-differentiable precisely when \(\Delta_tF\) has a graphical limit as \(t\downarrow0\); that limit is \(F'_{\bar x,\bar y}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional definition by graphical convergence of difference-quotient multifunctions.

source_refs.locator: 4.4 Sensitivity Analysis for Variational Systems p. 421
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(t>0\), define the difference-quotient multifunction
\[
\Delta_tF(u):=\frac{F(\bar x+tu)-\bar y}{t}.
\]
The multifunction \(F\) is proto-differentiable at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar y\) if a multifunction \(F'_{\bar x,\bar y}\) exists such that
\[
\Delta_tF\xrightarrow{g}F'_{\bar x,\bar y}\quad\text{as }t\downarrow0,
\]
where graphical convergence means Painlevé–Kuratowski convergence of the graphs. The limit \(F'_{\bar x,\bar y}\) is the proto-derivative; when it exists, its graph equals \(T_{\operatorname{gph}F}(\bar x,\bar y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proto-differentiability requires the scaled graph increments of a multifunction to converge graphically to a single derivative multifunction.
knowledge_statements.title: Proto-Derivatives

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The limiting second-order subdifferential of \(f\) at \(\bar x\) relative to \(\bar v\) is the multifunction \(\partial^2f(\bar x,\bar v):\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^n\) defined by
\[
\partial^2f(\bar x,\bar v)(u):=D^*(\partial f)(\bar x,\bar v)(u).
\]
Equivalently,
\[
w\in\partial^2f(\bar x,\bar v)(u)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
(w,-u)\in N_{\operatorname{gph}\partial f}(\bar x,\bar v).
\]
For a twice continuously differentiable finite-valued function, this set reduces to \(\{\nabla^2f(\bar x)u\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The limiting second-order subdifferential is the limiting coderivative of the first-order limiting subgradient mapping.
knowledge_statements.title: Limiting Second-Order Subdifferentials

source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The combined second-order subdifferential of \(f\) at \(\bar x\) relative to \(\bar v\) is defined by the regular coderivative of the limiting subgradient mapping:
\[
\breve\partial^{\,2}f(\bar x,\bar v)(u):=\widehat D^*(\partial f)(\bar x,\bar v)(u).
\]
Equivalently,
\[
w\in\breve\partial^{\,2}f(\bar x,\bar v)(u)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
(w,-u)\in\widehat N_{\operatorname{gph}\partial f}(\bar x,\bar v).
\]
It is mixed because the underlying first-order mapping is limiting while the normal used to differentiate its graph is regular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The combined second-order subdifferential applies the regular coderivative to the limiting subgradient mapping.
knowledge_statements.title: Combined Second-Order Subdifferentials

children.title: Clarke Generalized Hessians
children.top_down_role: Convexified generalized Hessian models for locally Lipschitz gradients.

assumptions_latex: \(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuously differentiable on an open set \(U\subset\mathbb{R}^n\).
\(\nabla f\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\in U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial_C^2f(\bar x)=\operatorname{co}\{\lim_k\nabla^2f(x_k):x_k\to\bar x,\ f\text{ twice differentiable at }x_k\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Clarke generalized Hessian for a locally Lipschitz gradient.

source_refs.locator: 7.1 Nonsmooth Analysis I: Clarke's Calculus p. 626
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Omega_f\) be the full-measure set on which the locally Lipschitz mapping \(\nabla f\) is differentiable. The Clarke generalized Hessian of \(f\) at \(\bar x\) is
\[
\partial_C^2f(\bar x):=\operatorname{co}\left\{H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\mid
\exists x_k\in\Omega_f,\ x_k\to\bar x,\ \nabla^2f(x_k)\to H\right\}.
\]
It is a nonempty compact convex set of symmetric matrices. If \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\), then \(\partial_C^2f(\bar x)=\{\nabla^2f(\bar x)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Clarke generalized Hessian is the convex hull of all limiting classical Hessians at nearby twice-differentiability points.
knowledge_statements.title: Clarke Generalized Hessians

\(\bar v\in\partial_x f(\bar x,\bar y)\).

notation.meaning: Limiting partial subdifferential in the first variable

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise limiting construction with the second variable held fixed in the coderivative input.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Regard the partial subgradient mapping as \(\partial_xf:\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^n\). Its first-variable partial second-order subdifferential at \(((\bar x,\bar y),\bar v)\) is
\[
\partial_{xx}^2f((\bar x,\bar y),\bar v)(u):=
\{w\in\mathbb{R}^n\mid (w,0)\in D^*(\partial_xf)((\bar x,\bar y),\bar v)(u)\}.
\]
The zero component suppresses dual variation in the second block. More generally, the full coderivative value \(D^*(\partial_xf)((\bar x,\bar y),\bar v)(u)\subset\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^p\) records coupled second-order effects in both variable blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partial second-order subdifferential extracts coderivative responses associated with one variable block while suppressing dual variation in the other block.
knowledge_statements.title: Partial Second-Order Subdifferentials

children.title: Prox-Regular Functions
children.top_down_role: Localized nonconvex functions retaining stable proximal geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
\((\bar x,\bar v)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f\) and \(f(\bar x)<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x')\ge f(x)+\langle v,x'-x\rangle-\tfrac r2\|x'-x\|^2\) locally along \(\operatorname{gph}\partial f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise prox-regularity relative to a designated limiting subgradient.

source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The function \(f\) is prox-regular at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\) if there exist \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(r\ge0\) such that
\[
f(x')\ge f(x)+\langle v,x'-x\rangle-\frac r2\|x'-x\|^2
\]
whenever \(\|x'-\bar x\|<\varepsilon\), \(\|x-\bar x\|<\varepsilon\), \(|f(x)-f(\bar x)|<\varepsilon\), and \(v\in\partial f(x)\) satisfies \(\|v-\bar v\|<\varepsilon\). If this holds for every \(\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)\), then \(f\) is prox-regular at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prox-regularity requires a uniform local quadratic lower support inequality for nearby subgradients and nearby points with compatible function values.
knowledge_statements.title: Prox-Regular Functions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lower-C2 Characterization via Prox-Regularity and Strict Continuity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularity implications and converse characterization on an open set, with a strictly differentiable local specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $O\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be open. If $f$ is lower-$\mathcal C^2$ on $O$, then $f$ is prox-regular and subdifferentially continuous at every point of $O$ and strictly continuous on $O$. Conversely, if $f$ is prox-regular and strictly continuous on $O$, then $f$ is lower-$\mathcal C^2$ on $O$. In particular, if $f$ is prox-regular at $\bar x$ and strictly differentiable at $\bar x$, then $f$ is lower-$\mathcal C^2$ on a neighborhood of $\bar x$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On an open set, every lower-C2 function is prox-regular and subdifferentially continuous at every point and is strictly continuous. Conversely, prox-regularity together with strict continuity on the set implies lower-C2 structure. Pointwise prox-regularity at a strictly differentiable point consequently yields lower-C2 structure nearby.
assumptions_latex: O\subset\mathbb{R}^n\text{ is open}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ lower-}\mathcal C^2\text{ on }O\Rightarrow f\text{ is prox-regular and subdifferentially continuous at every point of }O\text{ and strictly continuous on }O;\quad f\text{ prox-regular and strictly continuous on }O\Rightarrow f\text{ lower-}\mathcal C^2\text{ on }O.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Prox-Regularity of a Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise prox-regularity relative to a specified limiting subgradient, including the all-subgradients variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A function $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ is prox-regular at $\bar x$ for $\bar v$ if $f$ is finite and locally lower semicontinuous at $\bar x$, $\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)$, and there exist $\varepsilon>0$ and $\rho\geq0$ such that
\[
f(x')\geq f(x)+\langle v,x'-x\rangle-\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert x'-x\rVert^2
\]
for every $x'\in\mathbb B(\bar x,\varepsilon)$ whenever $v\in\partial f(x)$, $\lVert v-\bar v\rVert<\varepsilon$, $\lVert x-\bar x\rVert<\varepsilon$, and $f(x)<f(\bar x)+\varepsilon$. The function is prox-regular at $\bar x$ if this holds for every $\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function is prox-regular at x-bar for v-bar when it is finite and locally lower semicontinuous there and has a uniform local quadratic lower-support inequality at all nearby subdifferential graph points satisfying the stated value bound. It is prox-regular at x-bar when this holds for every subgradient there.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}
f(\bar x)\in\mathbb{R}\text{ and }f\text{ is locally lsc at }\bar x
\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\varepsilon>0,\ \rho\geq0\ \text{such that the stated quadratic support inequality holds for every }x'\text{ and every }(x,v)\text{ satisfying the specified conditions.}

source_evidence.locator: Second-Order Theory / F. Prox-Regularity / Definition 13.27

children.title: Subdifferential Continuity
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of function values with nearby subgradient graph behavior.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
\((\bar x,\bar v)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f\) and \(f(\bar x)<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x_k,v_k)\to(\bar x,\bar v),\ v_k\in\partial f(x_k)\Rightarrow f(x_k)\to f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential finite-dimensional definition relative to a designated limiting subgradient.

source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The function \(f\) is subdifferentially continuous at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\) if every sequence \((x_k,v_k)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f\) satisfying
\[
(x_k,v_k)\to(\bar x,\bar v)
\]
also satisfies
\[
f(x_k)\to f(\bar x).
\]
Equivalently, the value mapping \((x,v)\mapsto f(x)\), restricted to \(\operatorname{gph}\partial f\), is continuous at \((\bar x,\bar v)\). Subdifferential continuity at \(\bar x\) means that this condition holds for every \(\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nearby graph points of the subgradient mapping must carry function values converging to the reference value.
knowledge_statements.title: Subdifferential Continuity

\(\bar x\in C\) and \(\bar v\in N_C(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The second-order indicator model is the lower epigraphical limit of the displayed normalized feasibility quotients.

notation.meaning: Indicator of C, equal to zero on C and positive infinity elsewhere.
Second subderivative of the indicator relative to the normal vector.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the denominator \(t^2/2\) convention for second subderivatives.

source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The second subderivative of the indicator of \(C\) at \(\bar x\) relative to \(\bar v\) is
\[
d_e^2\delta_C(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w):=\liminf_{\substack{t\downarrow0\\w'\to w}}\frac{\delta_C(\bar x+tw')-\delta_C(\bar x)-t\langle\bar v,w'\rangle}{\tfrac12t^2}.
\]
Equivalently, only perturbations satisfying \(\bar x+tw'\in C\) contribute finite values. Thus the model records the second-order feasible approach geometry of \(C\) after subtracting the first-order normal term.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The indicator’s second subderivative measures second-order feasible approaches after removing the linear contribution of the reference normal.
knowledge_statements.title: Indicator-Function Second-Order Models

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(x\in C\), the limiting normal cone and indicator subdifferential satisfy
\[
N_C(x)=\partial\delta_C(x).

Their graphs and graphical derivatives therefore satisfy
\[
\operatorname{gph}N_C=\operatorname{gph}\partial\delta_C

\]

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard finite-dimensional epi-to-proto correspondence under prox-regularity and subdifferential continuity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional prox-regular epi-to-proto theorem with the \(t^2/2\) normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the stated assumptions, the difference-quotient mappings
\[
w\mapsto\frac{\partial f(\bar x+tw)-\bar v}{t}
\]
graphically converge as \(t\downarrow0\). Hence \(\partial f\) is proto-differentiable at \((\bar x,\bar v)\), and its proto-derivative is determined by the second epi-derivative:
\[
D(\partial f)(\bar x,\bar v)(w)=\partial\!\left(\frac12d_e^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)\right)(w)
\quad\text{for every }\(w\in\mathbb R^n\).
\]
The subdifferential on the right is taken with respect to the direction variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a twice epi-differentiable prox-regular function, the proto-derivative of its subgradient is the subgradient of half its second epi-derivative.
knowledge_statements.title: Subgradient Proto-Differentiability

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second Derivatives and Quadratic Expansions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the differentiable specialization of the subgradient proto-derivative correspondence for prox-regular functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}} be differentiable at \bar x and prox-regular there for \bar v=\nabla f(\bar x). The following are equivalent: (a) f is twice differentiable at \bar x in the extended sense; (b) \partial f is differentiable at \bar x; (c) f has a quadratic expansion at \bar x. When these conditions hold, \nabla^2f(\bar x) is symmetric and f is lower-\mathcal C^2 around \bar x.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a function differentiable at the point and prox-regular there for its gradient, extended twice differentiability, differentiability of the subgradient mapping, and existence of a quadratic expansion are equivalent. The resulting Hessian is symmetric, and the function is locally lower-C2.

f\text{ is differentiable at }\bar x
\bar v=\nabla f(\bar x)
f\text{ is prox-regular at }\bar x\text{ for }\bar v

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Proto-Differentiability and Twice Epi-Differentiability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes proto-differentiability of prox-regular subgradient mappings and identifies their proto-derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}} is prox-regular at \bar x for \bar v\in\partial f(\bar x) and is subdifferentially continuous there. Then \partial f is proto-differentiable at \bar x for \bar v if and only if f is twice epi-differentiable at \bar x for \bar v. In that case h=\tfrac12d^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v) is proper and \[D(\partial f)(\bar x\mid\bar v)=\partial h.\] Without subdifferential continuity, the same conclusions hold after replacing \partial f by any sufficiently close f-attentive localization at (\bar x,\bar v).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a prox-regular and subdifferentially continuous function, proto-differentiability of the subgradient mapping is equivalent to twice epi-differentiability of the function, and the proto-derivative is the subdifferential of half the second epi-derivative. Without subdifferential continuity, the conclusions apply to sufficiently close attentive localizations.

\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)
f\text{ is prox-regular at }\bar x\text{ for }\bar v
f\text{ is subdifferentially continuous at }\bar x\text{ for }\bar v\text{, unless an }f\text{-attentive localization is used}

children.title: Normal-Mapping Proto-Differentiability
children.top_down_role: Set-geometric specialization for normal-cone mappings.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is locally closed and prox-regular at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\in N_C(\bar x)\).
\(\delta_C\) is twice epi-differentiable at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_C\) is proto-differentiable at \((\bar x,\bar v)\) and \(DN_C(\bar x,\bar v)=\partial(\tfrac12d_e^2\delta_C(\bar x\mid\bar v))\).

notation.meaning: Graphical derivative of the normal-cone mapping.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: indicator specialization of the prox-regular epi-to-proto theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-indicator specialization of subgradient proto-differentiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the stated assumptions, the normal-cone difference quotients
\[
w\mapsto\frac{N_C(\bar x+tw)-\bar v}{t}
\]
graphically converge as \(t\downarrow0\). Therefore \(N_C\) is proto-differentiable at \((\bar x,\bar v)\), and for every \(w\in\mathbb R^n\),
\[
DN_C(\bar x,\bar v)(w)=\partial\!\left(\frac12d_e^2\delta_C(\bar x\mid\bar v)\right)(w).
\]
This identity transfers the second-order feasible geometry encoded by the indicator into the graphical derivative of the normal mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Twice epi-differentiability of a prox-regular set indicator yields proto-differentiability of the normal mapping and an explicit second-order representation.
knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Mapping Proto-Differentiability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem is the expected indicator specialization, but no source is supplied for the precise prox-regularity, continuity, twice epi-differentiability, and normalization assumptions. Those details are material to the conclusion.

children.title: Proximity-Mapping Differentiability
children.top_down_role: Proximity and resolvent consequences of epi-proto correspondence.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) satisfies the hypotheses ensuring the proto-derivative \(D(\partial f)(\bar x,\bar v)\).
\(\lambda>0\), \(\bar y=\bar x+\lambda\bar v\), and the resolvent \((I+\lambda\partial f)^{-1}\) is locally single-valued at \(\bar y\).
For each \(h\), the linearized inclusion has a unique solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_\lambda=(I+\lambda\partial f)^{-1}\) is directionally differentiable at \(\bar y\), with derivative determined by \(h\in w+\lambda D(\partial f)(\bar x,\bar v)(w)\).

notation.meaning: Directional derivative of the proximity mapping.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: directional differentiation of a locally single-valued resolvent of a proto-differentiable mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional derivative of a locally single-valued proximal resolvent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The proximity mapping satisfies
\[
P_\lambda=(I+\lambda\partial f)^{-1},\qquad P_\lambda(\bar y)=\bar x.
\]
Under the stated assumptions, \(P_\lambda\) is directionally differentiable at \(\bar y\). For every input direction \(h\in\mathbb R^n\), its derivative \(w=P_\lambda'(\bar y;h)\) is the unique vector satisfying
\[
h\in w+\lambda D(\partial f)(\bar x,\bar v)(w).
\]
If the epi-to-proto representation applies, the last term may equivalently be replaced by \(\lambda\partial(\tfrac12d_e^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v))(w)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The directional derivative of a locally single-valued proximity mapping solves the resolvent inclusion formed from the subgradient proto-derivative.
knowledge_statements.title: Proximity-Mapping Differentiability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The first assumption circularly refers to unspecified hypotheses, and local single-valuedness plus pointwise uniqueness of the linearized inclusion is not an inspectable standard hypothesis package for directional differentiability. An exact resolvent-differentiation theorem is required.

children.title: Second Epi-Differentiability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Epigraphical regimes supporting correspondence with mapping-level proto-differentiability.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
\(\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Twice epi-differentiability means that the second difference quotients epi-converge to the proper function \(d_e^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard finite-dimensional definition of twice epi-differentiability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional definition with denominator \(t^2/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(t>0\), define
\[
\Delta_t^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w):=\frac{f(\bar x+tw)-f(\bar x)-t\langle\bar v,w\rangle}{\tfrac12t^2}.
\]
The function \(f\) is twice epi-differentiable at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\) when there exists a proper lower-semicontinuous function \(q:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) such that
\[
\Delta_t^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)\xrightarrow{e}q\quad\text{as }\(t\downarrow0\).
\]
The limit is denoted by \(q=d_e^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Twice epi-differentiability is epigraphical convergence of normalized second-order difference quotients to a proper lower-semicontinuous model.
knowledge_statements.title: Second Epi-Differentiability Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind are plausible, but no citation supports the selected normalization and proper-limit convention. The second display also nests inline math delimiters inside display math.

children.title: Epi-to-Proto Transfer Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on transferring second epigraphical information to proto-derivative representations.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is defined by \(f(0)=0\) and \(f(x)=x^2\sin(1/x)\) for \(x\neq0\).
The reference pair is \((\bar x,\bar v)=(0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without prox-regularity, a second epi-derivative does not guarantee the proto-derivative identity for \(\partial f\).

notation.meaning: Second-order difference quotient at the reference pair.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oscillatory one-dimensional boundary example illustrating the role of prox-regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(w\neq0\),
\[
\Delta_t^2f(0\mid0)(w)=2w^2\sin\!\left(\frac1{tw}\right),
\]
whose oscillations permit an epigraphical lower model while the nearby derivatives
\[
f'(x)=2x\sin(1/x)-\cos(1/x)
\]
have order-one oscillations as \(x\to0\). Consequently the scaled subgradient graphs need not converge to the subgradient graph of half the second epi-model. Thus twice epi-differentiability alone, after prox-regularity is removed, does not imply the epi-to-proto identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An oscillatory quadratic can possess a second epi-model while its scaled subgradient graphs fail to obey the expected proto-derivative formula.
knowledge_statements.title: Epi-to-Proto Transfer Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The oscillatory calculations alone do not specify the epi-limit or an explicit graphical sequence proving failure of proto-differentiability or of the asserted identity. Because the validity of this particular counterexample is source-sensitive, an exact source or direct verified formulation is required.

children.top_down_role: One-sided relations between primal and dual derivative constructions.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^m\) has locally closed graph near \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\).
\(u,k\in\mathbb R^m\), \(z,h\in\mathbb R^n\), \(z\in\widehat D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(u)\), and \(k\in DF(\bar x,\bar y)(h)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle z,h\rangle\leq\langle u,k\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Universal polar inequality linking graphical derivatives and regular coderivatives.

source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For all \(h,z\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(k,u\in\mathbb R^m\),
\[
z\in\widehat D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(u)\ \text{ and }\ k\in DF(\bar x,\bar y)(h)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\langle z,h\rangle\leq\langle u,k\rangle.
\]
This is a one-sided primal-dual relation and does not generally identify either construction without additional graphical regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every regular-coderivative pair has nonpositive polar pairing with every graphical-derivative pair, equivalently the displayed primal-dual inequality holds.

children.title: Regularity-Based Identifications
children.top_down_role: Regimes where primal and dual representations determine common second-order information.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is single-valued and continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
\(\bar y=F(\bar x)\) and \(A=\nabla F(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(DF(\bar x,\bar y)(h)=\{Ah\}\) and \(D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(u)=\{A^{\mathsf T}u\}\).

notation.meaning: Jacobian of F at the reference point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth single-valued regime where primal and dual derivatives are adjoint.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The graph of \(F\) is locally a smooth manifold whose tangent and normal spaces are
\[
T_{\operatorname{gph}F}(\bar x,\bar y)=\{(h,Ah):h\in\mathbb R^n\}
\]
and
\[
N_{\operatorname{gph}F}(\bar x,\bar y)=\{(-A^{\mathsf T}u,u):u\in\mathbb R^m\}.
\]
Consequently, for every \(h\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(u\in\mathbb R^m\),
\[
DF(\bar x,\bar y)(h)=\{Ah\},\qquad D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(u)=\{A^{\mathsf T}u\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth single-valued mapping, the graphical derivative is its Jacobian and the coderivative is the transposed Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.title: Regularity-Based Identifications

children.title: Convex Second-Order Conjugacy
children.top_down_role: Duality between primal and conjugate second-order models.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
\(\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)\).
Both paired second epi-derivatives exist as proper closed convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\tfrac12d_e^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v))^*=\tfrac12d_e^2f^*(\bar v\mid\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugate of a directional model q.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex second-order Fenchel conjugacy under the \(t^2/2\) convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
q(w)=\frac12d_e^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w),
\qquad
q^*(z)=\sup_w\{\langle z,w\rangle-q(w)\}.
\]
Under the stated paired twice epi-differentiability assumptions, the conjugate second-order model is
\[
q^*(z)=\frac12d_e^2f^*(\bar v\mid\bar x)(z)
\quad\text{for every }\(z\in\mathbb R^n\).
\]
Thus primal and conjugate curvature models are Fenchel conjugates after the common factor \(1/2\) dictated by the selected second-difference normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex function and its conjugate, the paired half-scaled second epi-derivatives are Fenchel conjugates.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Second-Order Conjugacy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Second-order conjugacy is source-sensitive with respect to the difference-quotient normalization and the precise paired epi-convergence assumptions. No authoritative locator is supplied, and the display improperly nests inline delimiters inside display math.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-order epi-differentiability under convex conjugacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of proper twice epi-differentiability for a closed proper convex function and its conjugate, with conjugacy of the corresponding second epi-derivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}} be lower semicontinuous, proper, and convex. Let \bar{x}\in\operatorname{dom}f and \bar{v}\in\partial f(\bar{x}); equivalently, \bar{v}\in\operatorname{dom}f^* and \bar{x}\in\partial f^*(\bar{v}). Then f is properly twice epi-differentiable at \bar{x} for \bar{v} if and only if f^* is properly twice epi-differentiable at \bar{v} for \bar{x}. In that case, \frac12d^2f(\bar{x}\mid\bar{v}) and \frac12d^2f^*(\bar{v}\mid\bar{x}) are convex conjugates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a primal-dual subgradient pair of a lower-semicontinuous proper convex function, proper twice epi-differentiability holds for the function exactly when it holds for its conjugate at the reversed pair. When it holds, one half of their second epi-derivatives are convex conjugates.

\bar{x}\in\operatorname{dom}f
\bar{v}\in\partial f(\bar{x})
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is properly twice epi-differentiable at }\bar{x}\text{ for }\bar{v}\iff f^*\text{ is properly twice epi-differentiable at }\bar{v}\text{ for }\bar{x},\qquad \frac12d^2f(\bar{x}\mid\bar{v})=\left(\frac12d^2f^*(\bar{v}\mid\bar{x})\right)^*.

children.title: Subgradient-Graph Duality
children.top_down_role: Dual interpretation of subgradient proto-derivatives and second epi-derivatives.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
\(\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D(\partial f^*)(\bar v,\bar x)=[D(\partial f)(\bar x,\bar v)]^{-1}\).

notation.meaning: Graphical derivative of the subgradient mapping.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: graphical differentiation of the Fenchel subgradient inverse identity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph-swapping duality for convex subgradient proto-derivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fenchel subgradient duality gives
\[
\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\bar x\in\partial f^*(\bar v),
\qquad
(\partial f)^{-1}=\partial f^*.
\]
Swapping the coordinates of the two identical graphs also swaps their tangent directions. Hence
\[
z\in D(\partial f)(\bar x,\bar v)(w)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
w\in D(\partial f^*)(\bar v,\bar x)(z),
\]
or equivalently
\[
D(\partial f^*)(\bar v,\bar x)=[D(\partial f)(\bar x,\bar v)]^{-1}.
\]
When the epi-to-proto theorem applies, these inverse mappings are generated by the paired second epi-models.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex conjugacy swaps subgradient graph coordinates, so the graphical derivatives of the primal and conjugate subgradients are inverse mappings.
knowledge_statements.title: Subgradient-Graph Duality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The graph-inversion identity is standard and the duality content kind fits, but the record supplies no citation and includes a derivational argument rather than only a knowledge statement. An exact source should support the graphical-derivative inverse identity and its scope.

children.title: Primal–Dual Curvature Transfer
children.top_down_role: Transfer of curvature and growth information between conjugate representations.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite-dimensional, and \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)\), and \(f\) is twice epi-differentiable at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d_e^2 f^*(\bar v\mid\bar x)(z)=2\left(\tfrac12 d_e^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)\right)^*(z).\]

notation.meaning: second epi-derivative with denominator one-half times the squared step

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex conjugacy under the half-square normalization of second difference quotients.

source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(z\in X\), the second epi-derivative of the conjugate transfers the primal curvature by scaled Fenchel conjugacy:
\[d_e^2 f^*(\bar v\mid\bar x)(z)=2\sup_{w\in X}\left\{\langle z,w\rangle-\tfrac12 d_e^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)\right\}.\]
Thus finiteness, coercivity, and positive quadratic growth of the primal second-order model correspond respectively to domain, smoothness, and reciprocal curvature properties of the dual model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual second-order model is the appropriately scaled Fenchel conjugate of the primal model, transferring growth and curvature information between them.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Curvature Transfer

source_witnesses.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

children.title: Additive Second-Order Calculus
children.top_down_role: Second-order calculus for finite sums of variational functions.

assumptions_latex: \(f_i:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper closed convex functions, and one is continuous at a common domain point.
\(\bar v\in\partial(\sum_{i=1}^m f_i)(\bar x)\), and the functions are twice epi-differentiable for every relevant subgradient decomposition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d_e^2\!\left(\sum_i f_i\right)(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)=\inf_{\substack{v_i\in\partial f_i(\bar x)\\\sum_i v_i=\bar v}}\sum_i d_e^2f_i(\bar x\mid v_i)(w).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convex finite-sum rule with minimization over compatible subgradient decompositions.

source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\) and
\[\mathcal V(\bar x,\bar v)=\{(v_1,\ldots,v_m):v_i\in\partial f_i(\bar x),\ \sum_i v_i=\bar v\}.\]
Then, for every \(w\in X\),
\[d_e^2F(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)=\inf_{(v_i)\in\mathcal V(\bar x,\bar v)}\sum_{i=1}^m d_e^2f_i(\bar x\mid v_i)(w),\]
with the infimum equal to \(+\infty\) when \(\mathcal V(\bar x,\bar v)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The second-order model of a qualified convex sum is the infimum of component models over all subgradients summing to the reference subgradient.
knowledge_statements.title: Additive Second-Order Calculus

source_witnesses.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

children.title: Block-Separable Second-Order Calculus
children.top_down_role: Second-order calculus organized by independent variable blocks or components.

assumptions_latex: \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\) and \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\), with each \(f_i\) proper and lower semicontinuous.
Each \(f_i\) is twice epi-differentiable at \(\bar x_i\) for \(\bar v_i\in\partial f_i(\bar x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d_e^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)=\sum_{i=1}^m d_e^2f_i(\bar x_i\mid\bar v_i)(w_i).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact product-space rule for an uncoupled separable extended-real-valued function.

source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\bar x=(\bar x_1,\ldots,\bar x_m)\), \(\bar v=(\bar v_1,\ldots,\bar v_m)\), and every \(w=(w_1,\ldots,w_m)\in X\), separability gives
\[d_e^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)=\sum_{i=1}^m d_e^2f_i(\bar x_i\mid\bar v_i)(w_i).\]
Consequently, the effective domain of the product model is the Cartesian product of the component effective domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an uncoupled block-separable function, the second epi-derivative is exactly the sum of the blockwise second epi-derivatives.

assumptions_latex: \(f_i:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper lower-semicontinuous functions finite at \(\bar x\).
The limiting-subdifferential qualification \(\{(v_i):v_i\in\partial^\infty f_i(\bar x),\ \sum_i v_i=0\}\subseteq\{(0,\ldots,0)\}\) holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[\partial\!\left(\sum_i f_i\right)(\bar x)\subseteq\sum_i\partial f_i(\bar x),\]
with exact second-order sum rules requiring compatible twice epi-differentiability or second-order regularity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A standard finite-dimensional horizon qualification separating admissible coupled sums from abnormal cancellation.

source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A coupled finite sum satisfies the basic qualification at \(\bar x\) when
\[v_i\in\partial^\infty f_i(\bar x)\ \text{for all }i,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^m v_i=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad v_i=0\ \text{for all }i.\]
This excludes cancellation of abnormal horizon subgradients. Together with twice epi-differentiability and attainment of a compatible decomposition \(\bar v=\sum_i v_i\), it is a standard regime for exact or inclusion-form second-order sum calculus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sum qualification excludes cancellation among nonzero horizon subgradients; second-order regularity is additionally needed for exact curvature formulas.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[\Lambda(\bar x,\bar v)=\{y\in\partial g(F(\bar x)):F'(\bar x)^*y=\bar v\}.\]
Under a composite qualification ensuring exactness, every \(w\in X\) satisfies
\[d_e^2(g\circ F)(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)=\inf_{y\in\Lambda(\bar x,\bar v)}\left\{d_e^2g(F(\bar x)\mid y)(F'(\bar x)w)+\langle y,F''(\bar x)[w,w]\rangle\right\}.\]
The two terms represent transported outer curvature and curvature of the inner mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composite curvature is outer curvature along the linearized image plus the multiplier-weighted second derivative of the smooth inner mapping.

\[d_e^2\delta_C(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)=

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(h(x)=\tfrac12 d_C(x)^2\).
The metric projection \(P_C\) is directionally differentiable at \(\bar x\) in direction \(w\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[h''(\bar x;w)=\langle w,w-P_C'(\bar x;w)\rangle.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second directional derivative of the squared distance to a closed convex set.

source_refs.source_title: Modern Nonconvex Nondifferentiable Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonempty closed convex set, \(P_C\) is single-valued and
\[\nabla h(x)=x-P_C(x),\qquad h(x)=\tfrac12 d_C(x)^2.\]
If \(P_C'(\bar x;w)\) exists, then the second directional derivative of \(h\) exists and satisfies
\[h''(\bar x;w)=\langle w,w-P_C'(\bar x;w)\rangle.\]
Hence the second-order behavior of squared distance is determined by the directional sensitivity of the metric projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The squared-distance curvature equals the direction paired with its residual after differentiating the metric projection.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(t>0\), set \[\Delta_t^2f(\bar x\mid v)(w):=\frac{f(\bar x+tw)-f(\bar x)-t\langle v,w\rangle}{\tfrac12t^2}.\] The second subderivative is the lower epigraphical limit \[d^2f(\bar x\mid v)(w)=\liminf_{\substack{t\downarrow0\\w'\to w}}\Delta_t^2f(\bar x\mid v)(w').\] Consequently, a second-subderivative calculus rule is obtained by transforming these quotients and passing to an epigraphical lower limit; an exact rule additionally requires matching recovery sequences, equivalently the corresponding epigraphical upper bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Epi-Derivative Calculus Architecture
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential finite-dimensional definition of proper twice epi-differentiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(t>0\), define \[\Delta_t^2f(\bar x\mid v)(w):=\frac{f(\bar x+tw)-f(\bar x)-t\langle v,w\rangle}{\tfrac12t^2}.\] The function \(f\) is properly twice epi-differentiable at \(\bar x\) for \(v\) when these quotients epigraphically converge as \(t\downarrow0\) to a proper extended-real function \(d_e^2f(\bar x\mid v)\). Equivalently, the epigraphical lower bound holds along every convergent sequence, and each \(w\in\mathbb{R}^n\) admits a recovery sequence attaining the matching upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proper twice epi-differentiability means that the second-order difference quotients epi-converge to a proper second epi-derivative.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is proper and lower semicontinuous, \(f(\bar x)<+\infty\), and \(v\in\partial f(\bar x)\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D^*(G\circ F)(\bar x,\bar z)(z^*)\subseteq\bigcup_{\bar y\in M(\bar x,\bar z)}D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(D^*G(\bar y,\bar z)(z^*))\).

notation.meaning: Set of intermediate points realizing the composition.
Image of a set under the set-valued coderivative.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional limiting-coderivative chain rule with intermediate-point compactness and qualification.

source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H:=G\circ F\) and \((\bar x,\bar z)\in\operatorname{gph}H\). Under the stated assumptions, for every \(z^*\in\mathbb R^p\),
\[
D^*H(\bar x,\bar z)(z^*)
\subseteq
\bigcup_{\bar y\in M(\bar x,\bar z)}
\bigcup_{y^*\in D^*G(\bar y,\bar z)(z^*)}
D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*).
\]
Thus each output covector is propagated first through \(G\) and then through \(F\), with a union over admissible intermediate points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A qualified coderivative chain rule propagates covectors backward through the outer and inner multifunctions, accounting for every locally relevant intermediate point.

assumptions_latex: \(F,G:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are \(C^1\) near \(\bar x\).
\(Q:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^p\) is \(C^1\) near \(F(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(D^*(F+G)( ar x)(y^*)=\{(
abla F( ar x)+
abla G( ar x))^	op y^*\}\) and \(D^*(Q\circ F)( ar x)(z^*)=\{
abla F( ar x)^	op
abla Q(F( ar x))^	op z^*\}\).

notation.meaning: Coderivative of a single-valued mapping, with its value suppressed.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth single-valued exactness regime for limiting-coderivative sum and chain rules.

source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a single-valued \(C^1\) mapping, its limiting coderivative is exactly the transpose Jacobian. Hence, for every \(y^*\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(z^*\in\mathbb R^p\),
\[
D^*(F+G)(\bar x)(y^*)=\{(\nabla F(\bar x)+\nabla G(\bar x))^\top y^*\},
\]
and
\[
D^*(Q\circ F)(\bar x)(z^*)=\{\nabla F(\bar x)^\top\nabla Q(F(\bar x))^\top z^*\}.
\]
Thus both coderivative calculus inclusions become equalities in the smooth single-valued regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For continuously differentiable single-valued mappings, coderivatives are transpose Jacobians, and the coderivative sum and chain rules are exact.

knowledge_statements.title: Inverse-Mapping Derivative Calculus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact graphical-derivative inversion identity in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^m\) and \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\). For every \(k\in\mathbb R^m\),
\[
DF^{-1}(\bar y,\bar x)(k)
=
\{h\in\mathbb R^n\mid k\in DF(\bar x,\bar y)(h)\}.
\]
Equivalently, \(h\in DF^{-1}(\bar y,\bar x)(k)\) if and only if \((h,k)\in T_{\operatorname{gph}F}(\bar x,\bar y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The graphical derivative of an inverse multifunction is obtained exactly by exchanging the input and output direction coordinates in the original graphical derivative.

assumptions_latex: \(g:\mathbb R^q\times\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is \(C^1\) near \((\bar p,\bar x)\) and \(g(\bar p,\bar x)=0\).
\(\nabla_x g(\bar p,\bar x):\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is surjective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(DS(\bar p,\bar x)(d)=\{u\in\mathbb R^n\mid \nabla_p g(\bar p,\bar x)d+\nabla_x g(\bar p,\bar x)u=0\}\).

notation.meaning: Solution multifunction of the parameterized equation.
Graphical derivative of the solution mapping.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth equation specialization under a surjective state Jacobian.

source_refs.locator: 4.4 Sensitivity Analysis for Variational Systems p. 421
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(S(p):=\{x\in\mathbb R^n\mid g(p,x)=0\}\). The surjectivity assumption makes the local zero set a smooth manifold. For every parameter direction \(d\in\mathbb R^q\), its solution-map graphical derivative is
\[
DS(\bar p,\bar x)(d)
=
\{u\in\mathbb R^n\mid
\nabla_p g(\bar p,\bar x)d+
\nabla_x g(\bar p,\bar x)u=0\}.
\]
Thus admissible solution velocities are precisely the solutions of the linearized implicit equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a surjective state Jacobian, the derivative of an implicit solution mapping consists exactly of velocities satisfying the linearized equation.
