knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\) has the Aubin property around \((\bar p,\bar x)\) if and only if \(D^*S(\bar p,\bar x)(0)=\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: Limiting coderivative of the solution mapping.

source_refs.locator: 4.4 Sensitivity Analysis for Variational Systems p. 421

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The mapping \(S\) has the Aubin property around \((\bar p,\bar x)\), meaning that there are neighborhoods \(U,V\) and \(L\geq0\) such that
\[
S(p_1)\cap V\subseteq S(p_2)+L\|p_1-p_2\|\mathbb B
\quad\text{for all }p_1,p_2\in U,
\]
if and only if the coderivative kernel condition
\[
D^*S(\bar p,\bar x)(0)=\{0\}
\]
holds. This characterizes the locally Lipschitz-like solution-mapping regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally closed solution mapping is Lipschitz-like exactly when its limiting coderivative maps the zero covector only to zero.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial^2 f(\bar x)(u)=\{\nabla^2 f(\bar x)u\}\) for every \(u\in\mathbb R^n\).

notation.meaning: Limiting second-order subdifferential, defined as the coderivative of the gradient mapping.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical \(C^2\) specialization of the limiting second-order subdifferential.

source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every direction \(u\in\mathbb R^n\), the limiting second-order subdifferential of \(f\) at \(\bar x\) is the singleton
\[
\partial^2 f(\bar x)(u)
:=D^*(\nabla f)(\bar x)(u)
=\{\nabla^2 f(\bar x)u\}.
\]
Hence all coderivative-based second-order information reduces to multiplication by the classical symmetric Hessian in the twice continuously differentiable regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a twice continuously differentiable function, the generalized second-order subdifferential is exactly the classical Hessian applied to the direction.

children.title: C1,1 Functions
children.top_down_role: Locally Lipschitz-gradient generalized Hessian representations.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is \(C^{1,1}\) near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial_C^2 f(\bar x)(u)=\{Au\mid A\in\partial_C(\nabla f)(\bar x)\}\) for every \(u\in\mathbb R^n\).

notation.meaning: Clarke generalized Jacobian of the locally Lipschitz gradient.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clarke generalized-Hessian representation for locally Lipschitz gradients.

source_refs.locator: 7.1 Nonsmooth Analysis I: Clarke's Calculus p. 626
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Since \(\nabla f\) is locally Lipschitz, it is differentiable almost everywhere. Its Clarke generalized Hessian is
\[
\partial_C(\nabla f)(\bar x)
=
\operatorname{co}\left\{\lim_{k\to\infty}\nabla^2f(x_k)
\mid x_k\to\bar x,\ \nabla f\text{ is differentiable at }x_k\right\}.
\]
For every \(u\in\mathbb R^n\), the associated second-order action is
\[
\partial_C^2 f(\bar x)(u)
=
\{Au\mid A\in\partial_C(\nabla f)(\bar x)\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a function with locally Lipschitz gradient, generalized Hessian actions are obtained by applying convexified limiting classical Hessians to the direction.
knowledge_statements.title: C1,1 Functions

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegativity of the second subderivative for proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(w\in\mathbb R^n\), define
\[
d^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)
:=
\liminf_{\substack{t\downarrow0\\w'\to w}}
\frac{f(\bar x+tw')-f(\bar x)-t\langle\bar v,w'\rangle}{\tfrac12t^2}.
\]
Then
\[
d^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)\geq0
\quad\text{for every }w\in\mathbb R^n.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper lower-semicontinuous convex function and any selected convex subgradient, the second subderivative is nonnegative in every direction.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
\(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)\).

children.title: Convex Piecewise-Linear Functions
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral epigraph and critical-face geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and piecewise linear.
\(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)=\delta_{K_f(\bar x,\bar v)}\).

notation.meaning: Critical cone determined by the directional derivative and subgradient.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Critical-cone formula for the second subderivative of a convex piecewise-linear function.

source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the critical cone
\[
K_f(\bar x,\bar v)
:=\{w\in\mathbb R^n\mid f'(\bar x;w)=\langle\bar v,w\rangle\}.
\]
Then the second subderivative has the exact polyhedral representation
\[
d^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)
=
\delta_{K_f(\bar x,\bar v)}(w)
=
\begin{cases}
0,&w\in K_f(\bar x,\bar v),\\
+\infty,&w\notin K_f(\bar x,\bar v).
\end{cases}
\]
Thus its finite directions are precisely the critical directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex piecewise-linear function, the second subderivative is zero on the critical cone and infinite outside it.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Piecewise-Linear Functions

children.title: Piecewise Linear-Quadratic Functions
children.top_down_role: Finite quadratic-piece second-order geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and piecewise linear-quadratic.
\(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is twice epi-differentiable at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\), and \(d^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and piecewise linear-quadratic.

notation.meaning: Second subderivative relative to the selected subgradient.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex piecewise linear-quadratic second-order closure property.

source_refs.source_title: Modern Nonconvex Nondifferentiable Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(t>0\), set
\[
\Delta_t^2f(w):=
\frac{f(\bar x+tw)-f(\bar x)-t\langle\bar v,w\rangle}{\tfrac12t^2}.
\]
As \(t\downarrow0\), these functions epi-converge to \(d^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)\); hence \(f\) is twice epi-differentiable at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\). Moreover, \(d^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)\) is a proper lower-semicontinuous convex piecewise linear-quadratic function, so its finite second-order geometry is described by finitely many polyhedral quadratic pieces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex piecewise linear-quadratic function is twice epi-differentiable, and its second subderivative remains a proper convex piecewise linear-quadratic function.
knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise Linear-Quadratic Functions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-order structure of convex piecewise linear-quadratic functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-subderivative evaluations, regularity regimes, failure at boundary points, and exact local expansions for convex PLQ functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}} is proper, convex, and piecewise linear-quadratic, and let \bar x\in\operatorname{dom}f. Then d^2f(\bar x) is proper and piecewise linear-quadratic, although not necessarily convex, and\[
d^2f(\bar x)(w)=\lim_{\tau\searrow0}\Delta_\tau^2f(\bar x)(w)=f''(\bar x;w)\geq0.
\]For v\in\partial f(\bar x), let\[
K(\bar x,v)=\{w:df(\bar x)(w)=\langle v,w\rangle\}.
\]This is a polyhedral cone, d^2f(\bar x\mid v) is proper, convex, and piecewise linear-quadratic, and\[
d^2f(\bar x\mid v)(w)=\lim_{\tau\searrow0}\Delta_\tau^2f(\bar x\mid v)(w)=d^2f(\bar x)(w)+\delta_{K(\bar x,v)}(w).
\]The function f is twice epi-differentiable at \bar x for every v\in\partial f(\bar x). It is twice semidifferentiable at \bar x when \bar x\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f), but not when \bar x\in\operatorname{bdry}(\operatorname{dom}f). Nevertheless, some neighborhood V of \bar x satisfies\[
f(x)=f(\bar x)+df(\bar x)(x-\bar x)+\tfrac12d^2f(\bar x)(x-\bar x)
\quad(x\in V\cap\operatorname{dom}f).
\]Moreover, there is \varepsilon>0 such that, for w\in T_{\operatorname{dom}f}(\bar x)\cap\mathbb B, \tau\in(0,\varepsilon), and z\in\mathbb{R}^n,\[
df(\bar x+\tau w)(z)=dh_1(w)(z)+\tfrac12\tau\,dh_2(w)(z),
\qquad h_1=df(\bar x),\quad h_2=d^2f(\bar x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper convex piecewise linear-quadratic function, the ordinary second subderivative is proper and PLQ, may be nonconvex, is nonnegative, and is obtained by fixed-direction limits. Relative to any subgradient, the second subderivative is proper convex PLQ and equals the ordinary second subderivative plus the indicator of the polyhedral critical cone. Twice epi-differentiability always holds for such subgradients. Twice semidifferentiability holds at interior domain points and fails at boundary points, although exact local function and directional-derivative expansions still hold on the domain.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\text{ is proper, convex, and piecewise linear-quadratic}
\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}f
v\in\partial f(\bar x)\text{ for the covector-relative conclusions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d^2f(\bar x)(w)=f''(\bar x;w)\geq0,\quad d^2f(\bar x\mid v)=d^2f(\bar x)+\delta_{K(\bar x,v)},\quad f\text{ is twice epi-differentiable for every }v\in\partial f(\bar x),\quad \bar x\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\Rightarrow f\text{ is twice semidifferentiable},\quad \bar x\in\operatorname{bdry}(\operatorname{dom}f)\Rightarrow f\text{ is not twice semidifferentiable}.

children.title: Polyhedral Normal-Cone Mappings
children.top_down_role: Critical-face representations for polyhedral systems.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a nonempty convex polyhedral set.
\((\bar x,\bar v)\in\operatorname{gph}N_C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(DN_C(\bar x,\bar v)(w)=N_K(w)\) for every \(w\in\mathbb{R}^n\).

notation.meaning: Critical cone at the reference normal pair.
Graphical derivative of the normal-cone mapping.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex-polyhedral graphical-derivative formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, convex, and polyhedral, and let \((\bar x,\bar v)\in\operatorname{gph}N_C\). Define the critical cone by \(K:=T_C(\bar x)\cap\bar v^\perp\). Then the graphical derivative of the convex normal-cone mapping has the exact representation
\[
DN_C(\bar x,\bar v)(w)=N_K(w)\qquad(w\in\mathbb{R}^n),
\]
where \(N_K(w)=\varnothing\) when \(w\notin K\). Thus evaluating the first-order graphical variation of \(N_C\), which supplies a basic second-order object for \(\delta_C\), reduces to evaluating normals to the polyhedral critical cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The graphical derivative of a polyhedral normal-cone mapping is exactly the normal-cone mapping of its critical cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Normal-Cone Mappings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is standard and fits the polyhedral-normal-cone leaf, but no source or inspectable locator is cited.

children.title: Smooth Nonlinear Constraint Systems
children.top_down_role: Multiplier and critical-cone evaluation for smooth constraints.

assumptions_latex: \(G:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^q\) is twice continuously differentiable and \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^q\) is convex polyhedral.
The constraint system \(G(x)\in D\) is nondegenerate at \(\bar x\), and the multiplier associated with \(\bar v\) is unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(DN_\Gamma(\bar x,\bar v)(w)=\nabla^2\langle\bar\lambda,G\rangle(\bar x)w+N_K(w)\).

notation.meaning: Feasible set of the smooth constraint system.
Unique multiplier satisfying the normal representation.
Critical cone of the feasible set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nondegenerate smooth constraints with a polyhedral target and unique multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Gamma:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:G(x)\in D\}\), where \(G\) is twice continuously differentiable and \(D\) is convex polyhedral. Suppose the constraint system is nondegenerate at \(\bar x\in\Gamma\). For \(\bar v\in N_\Gamma(\bar x)\), let \(\bar\lambda\in N_D(G(\bar x))\) be the unique multiplier satisfying \(\nabla G(\bar x)^*\bar\lambda=\bar v\), and set \(K:=T_\Gamma(\bar x)\cap\bar v^\perp\). Then
\[
DN_\Gamma(\bar x,\bar v)(w)=\nabla^2\langle\bar\lambda,G\rangle(\bar x)w+N_K(w).
\]
The right-hand side is empty whenever \(w\notin K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under nondegeneracy, the normal-map derivative equals the Lagrangian curvature term plus the normal cone to the critical cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Nonlinear Constraint Systems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the leaf, but the precise nondegeneracy condition and exact graphical-derivative formula require an authoritative source with a theorem or section locator.

children.title: Smooth-Composite Constraint Systems
children.top_down_role: Second-order reduction through smooth mappings and structured target sets.

assumptions_latex: \(G:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^q\) is twice continuously differentiable and \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^q\) is closed.
A second-order normal-cone chain rule holds at \((\bar x,\bar v)\), with a unique multiplier \(\bar\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(DN_\Gamma( ar x, ar v)(w)=
abla^2\langle ar\lambda,Gangle( ar x)w+
abla G( ar x)^*DN_D(G( ar x), ar\lambda)(
abla G( ar x)w)\).

notation.meaning: Graphical derivative of the target normal mapping.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact graphical-derivative reduction under an explicit second-order chain-rule qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Gamma:=G^{-1}(D)\), where \(G:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^q\) is twice continuously differentiable and \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^q\) is closed. Fix \((\bar x,\bar v)\in\operatorname{gph}N_\Gamma\), and suppose the applicable normal-cone chain rule is exact and yields a unique \(\bar\lambda\in N_D(G(\bar x))\) with \(\nabla G(\bar x)^*\bar\lambda=\bar v\). If its second-order graphical-derivative qualification also holds, then
\[
DN_\Gamma(\bar x,\bar v)(w)=\nabla^2\langle\bar\lambda,G\rangle(\bar x)w+\nabla G(\bar x)^*DN_D(G(\bar x),\bar\lambda)(\nabla G(\bar x)w).
\]
Hence all nonsmooth curvature is transferred to the structured target set \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A qualified smooth-composite system reduces normal-map differentiation to smooth Lagrangian curvature and the target set's normal-map derivative.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal-map derivative on the smooth nonzero boundary of one Lorentz cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q:=\{(t,u):t\geq\|u\|\}\), take \(x=(t,u)\in\partial Q\setminus\{0\}\), and put \(q:=u/t\). Every \(y\in N_Q(x)\) has the form \(y=\alpha(-1,q)\) with \(\alpha\geq0\). Define \(K:=T_Q(x)\cap y^\perp\) and the linear curvature operator \(\mathcal H_x(s,z):=(0,(I-qq^\top)z/t)\). Then
\[
DN_Q(x,y)(w)=\alpha\mathcal H_xw+N_K(w).
\]
Thus the second-order-cone normal derivative separates into boundary curvature and a critical-cone normal term; the formula also covers \(\alpha=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a nonzero Lorentz-cone boundary point, the normal derivative splits into explicit boundary curvature and a critical-cone normal.
knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Cone Systems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The boundary-curvature representation fits second-order cone systems, but its sign, scaling, and inclusion of the zero-multiplier case need an authoritative locator.

children.title: Semidefinite Constraint Systems
children.top_down_role: Spectral curvature and normal-map evaluation for positive-semidefinite cones.

assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb{S}_+^m\) and \(W\in T_{\mathbb{S}_+^m}(X)\).
The columns of \(P_0\) form an orthonormal basis of \(\ker X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T^2_{\mathbb{S}_+^m}(X,W)=\{Z:P_0^\top(Z-2WX^\dagger W)P_0\in T_{\mathbb{S}_+^r}(P_0^\top WP_0)\}\).

notation.meaning: Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse of the base matrix.
Orthonormal matrix spanning the kernel of the base matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer second-order tangent geometry of the positive-semidefinite cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\in\mathbb{S}_+^m\), let \(W\in T_{\mathbb{S}_+^m}(X)\), and let the columns of \(P_0\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times r}\) form an orthonormal basis of \(\ker X\). With \(X^\dagger\) denoting the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse, the outer second-order tangent set satisfies
\[
T^2_{\mathbb{S}_+^m}(X,W)=\left\{Z\in\mathbb{S}^m:P_0^\top(Z-2WX^\dagger W)P_0\in T_{\mathbb{S}_+^r}(P_0^\top WP_0)\right\}.
\]
The correction \(2WX^\dagger W\) is the spectral curvature generated by coupling the nullspace and positive-eigenvalue subspaces of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PSD second-order feasibility is determined on the kernel after subtracting an explicit pseudoinverse-based spectral curvature correction.
knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Constraint Systems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The PSD spectral-curvature representation fits the leaf, but the factor two and outer second-order tangent convention require a specific source locator.

children.title: Spectral Matrix-Mapping Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Eigenvalue- and singular-value-based second-order evaluation.

children.title: Eigenvalue-Based Second-Order Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Second-order evaluation organized through eigenvalue-dependent spectral structure.

assumptions_latex: \(A,H\in\mathbb{S}^m\).
\(\lambda_i(A)\) is simple, with orthonormal eigenvectors \(u_1,\ldots,u_m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\frac{d^2}{dt^2}\lambda_i(A+tH)|_{t=0}=2\sum_{j\ne i}\frac{|u_j^\top Hu_i|^2}{\lambda_i(A)-\lambda_j(A)}\).

notation.meaning: Ordered eigenvalues of the symmetric matrix.
Orthonormal eigenvectors of the symmetric matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical simple-eigenvalue second derivative along an affine symmetric-matrix path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A,H\in\mathbb{S}^m\), and suppose \(\lambda_i(A)\) is simple. Choose an orthonormal eigenbasis \(u_1,\ldots,u_m\) satisfying \(Au_j=\lambda_j(A)u_j\). Then the eigenvalue branch through \(\lambda_i(A)\) is twice differentiable along \(A+tH\), with
\[
\left.\frac{d}{dt}\lambda_i(A+tH)\right|_{t=0}=u_i^\top Hu_i,
\qquad
\left.\frac{d^2}{dt^2}\lambda_i(A+tH)\right|_{t=0}=2\sum_{j\ne i}\frac{|u_j^\top Hu_i|^2}{\lambda_i(A)-\lambda_j(A)}.
\]
The denominators encode the spectral-gap dependence of the second-order evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simple eigenvalue's second directional derivative is an explicit spectral-gap-weighted sum of squared cross-eigenspace couplings.
knowledge_statements.title: Eigenvalue-Based Second-Order Evaluation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The simple-eigenvalue formulas are mathematically standard and appropriately classified as a representation, but the record supplies no citation.

children.title: Singular-Value-Based Second-Order Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Second-order evaluation organized through singular-value-dependent spectral structure.

assumptions_latex: \(A,H\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\).
\(\sigma_i(A)>0\) is simple.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\frac{d^2}{dt^2}\sigma_i(A+tH)|_{t=0}=2\sum_{k\ne i}\frac{|z_k^\top\mathcal B(H)z_i|^2}{\sigma_i(A)-\theta_k}\).

notation.meaning: Symmetric dilation of a rectangular matrix.
Simple positive singular value under evaluation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simple positive singular value evaluated through symmetric dilation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(A,H\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), define the symmetric dilation \(\mathcal B(A):=\begin{pmatrix}0&A\\A^\top&0\end{pmatrix}\). Suppose \(\sigma_i(A)>0\) is simple, so it is a simple eigenvalue of \(\mathcal B(A)\). Let \((\theta_k,z_k)\) be an orthonormal eigenbasis of \(\mathcal B(A)\), indexed so that \(\theta_i=\sigma_i(A)\). Then
\[
\left.\frac{d^2}{dt^2}\sigma_i(A+tH)\right|_{t=0}=2\sum_{k\ne i}\frac{|z_k^\top\mathcal B(H)z_i|^2}{\sigma_i(A)-\theta_k}.
\]
This converts singular-value second-order evaluation into the corresponding symmetric eigenvalue calculation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The second derivative of a simple positive singular value is obtained by applying the simple-eigenvalue formula to the symmetric dilation.
knowledge_statements.title: Singular-Value-Based Second-Order Evaluation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The symmetric-dilation reduction fits the terminal container, but the complete dilation-spectrum indexing and formula need a cited authoritative locator.

children.title: Matrix-Valued Mapping Geometry
children.top_down_role: Second-order geometry associated with structured mappings taking matrix values.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{S}^m\) is twice continuously differentiable and \(K\subset\mathbb{S}^m\) is closed.
A second-order tangent inverse-image qualification holds at \(\bar x\in F^{-1}(K)\) in direction \(w\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T^2_{F^{-1}(K)}(\bar x,w)=\{z:F'(\bar x)z+F''(\bar x)[w,w]\in T^2_K(F(\bar x),F'(\bar x)w)\}\).

notation.meaning: Feasible inverse image of the matrix set.
First derivative of the matrix-valued mapping.
Second derivative evaluated twice in the direction.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order tangent chain rule for a smooth matrix-valued inverse image.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{S}^m\) be twice continuously differentiable, let \(K\subset\mathbb{S}^m\) be closed, and set \(\Gamma:=F^{-1}(K)\). Fix \(\bar x\in\Gamma\) and \(w\in T_\Gamma(\bar x)\). Under a qualification ensuring exact second-order tangent calculus for this inverse image,
\[
T^2_\Gamma(\bar x,w)=\left\{z\in\mathbb{R}^n:F'(\bar x)z+F''(\bar x)[w,w]\in T^2_K(F(\bar x),F'(\bar x)w)\right\}.
\]
Consequently, matrix-valued constraint curvature consists of the intrinsic second-order geometry of \(K\) combined with the acceleration \(F''(\bar x)[w,w]\) of the mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Qualified second-order feasibility for a matrix-valued constraint is the pullback of target-set second-order geometry plus mapping acceleration.
knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Valued Mapping Geometry

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inverse-image representation fits matrix-valued mapping geometry, but 'a qualification ensuring exact calculus' does not state checkable hypotheses; a source is needed to select the valid theorem version.

children.title: Spectral Multiplicity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Evaluation regimes distinguished by simple, repeated, or changing spectral values.

assumptions_latex: \(A(t)=A+tH+\tfrac12t^2K+o(t^2)\) in \(\mathbb{S}^m\).
\(\lambda\) is an eigenvalue of \(A\) with eigenspace basis \(U\), and \(V\) spans a selected eigenspace of \(U^\top HU\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The second derivatives in that first-order subcluster are the eigenvalues of \(V^\top U^\top[K+2H(\lambda I-A)^\dagger H]UV\).

notation.meaning: Orthonormal basis matrix for the repeated-eigenvalue eigenspace.
Basis for an eigenspace of the first-order compression.
Moore-Penrose inverse on the complement of the eigenspace.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeated symmetric eigenvalues resolved first by compression, then by a second compressed operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A(t)=A+tH+\tfrac12t^2K+o(t^2)\) with symmetric \(A,H,K\), and let \(\lambda\) be an eigenvalue of \(A\) whose eigenspace has orthonormal basis matrix \(U\). The first derivatives of the eigenvalue branches issuing from \(\lambda\) are the eigenvalues of \(U^\top HU\). Fix such a derivative \(\mu\), and let \(V\) span the corresponding eigenspace of \(U^\top HU\). The second derivatives of the branches in this subcluster are the eigenvalues of
\[
V^\top U^\top\left[K+2H(\lambda I-A)^\dagger H\right]UV.
\]
Thus multiplicity requires successive diagonalization within nested active spectral subspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a repeated eigenvalue, first derivatives come from one compression; each tied first-order cluster is resolved by a curvature-corrected second compression.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Multiplicity Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Successive compression is appropriate for spectral multiplicity regimes, but the branch-ordering convention and curvature operator require an authoritative theorem locator.

children.title: Unconstrained Second-Order Necessity
children.top_down_role: Necessary-condition families for extended-real unconstrained minimization.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and \(\bar x\) is a finite local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\widehat\partial f(\bar x)\) and \(d^2f(\bar x\mid0)(w)\geq0\) for every \(w\in\mathbb{R}^n\).

notation.meaning: Second subderivative relative to the zero subgradient.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-real local minimum using the lower second subderivative normalized by one-half squared step length.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, and suppose \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer with \(f(\bar x)<+\infty\). Then \(0\in\widehat\partial f(\bar x)\). With the second subderivative defined by
\[
d^2f(\bar x\mid0)(w):=\liminf_{\substack{t\downarrow0\\w'\to w}}\frac{f(\bar x+tw')-f(\bar x)}{\tfrac12t^2},
\]
one has
\[
d^2f(\bar x\mid0)(w)\geq0\qquad\text{for every }w\in\mathbb{R}^n.
\]
The value \(+\infty\) is permitted, so the condition applies without assuming twice epi-differentiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every finite local minimizer has zero as a regular subgradient, and its lower second subderivative relative to zero is nonnegative in every direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Unconstrained Second-Order Necessity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits unconstrained second-order necessity and is precise under its displayed normalization, but no source supports the stated extended-real version.

For \(w\in T_C( ar x)\) with \(\langle
abla f( ar x),wangle=0\) and \(z\in T_C^2( ar x,w)\), \(\langle

abla^2f( ar x)wangle\geq0\).

notation.meaning: Outer second-order tangent set in direction w.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric necessity along parabolically feasible arcs for a smooth objective over a closed set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed, let \(f\) be twice continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\in C\), and suppose \(\bar x\) locally minimizes \(f\) over \(C\). If \(w\in T_C(\bar x)\) satisfies \(\langle\nabla f(\bar x),w\rangle=0\), then every \(z\in T_C^2(\bar x,w)\), under the convention \(\bar x+tw+\tfrac12t^2z+o(t^2)\in C\), satisfies
\[
\langle\nabla f(\bar x),z\rangle+\langle w,\nabla^2f(\bar x)w\rangle\geq0.
\]
Thus objective curvature and second-order feasible displacement must be jointly nonnegative along each first-order critical direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Along every critical feasible direction, objective Hessian curvature plus the gradient applied to any second-order feasible displacement must be nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.title: Set-Constrained Second-Order Necessity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem matches set-constrained necessity, but the outer second-order tangent convention and claimed quantification over all such displacements need a cited theorem or section.

children.title: Critical-Cone Second-Order Necessity
children.top_down_role: Directional necessary-condition families on first-order critical directions.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is closed, \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\in C\), and \(\bar x\) locally minimizes \(f\) over \(C\).
The stationarity condition \(\bar v:=-\nabla f(\bar x)\in N_C(\bar x)\) holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle w,\nabla^2f(\bar x)w\rangle+d^2\delta_C(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)\geq0\) for every \(w\in K\).

notation.meaning: Critical cone for the stationary normal.
Second subderivative of the indicator relative to the stationary normal.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Critical-cone condition expressed through the second subderivative of the constraint indicator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed, let \(f\) be twice continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\in C\), and suppose \(\bar x\) locally minimizes \(f\) over \(C\). Assume stationarity with \(\bar v:=-\nabla f(\bar x)\in N_C(\bar x)\), and define \(K:=T_C(\bar x)\cap\bar v^\perp\). Then the second-order necessary condition for the extended-real objective \(f+\delta_C\) is
\[
\langle w,\nabla^2f(\bar x)w\rangle+d^2\delta_C(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)\geq0
\qquad(w\in K).
\]
Directions outside \(K\) do not furnish first-order critical feasible variations and are excluded from this directional test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On every critical direction, smooth objective curvature plus the constraint indicator's second subderivative must be nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.title: Critical-Cone Second-Order Necessity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits critical-cone necessity, but the normal-cone type and second-subderivative conventions must be fixed and supported by an authoritative locator.

children.title: Multiplier-Dependent Second-Order Necessity

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\le0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\) and \(h_j(x)=0\) for \(j=1,\ldots,p\). Let \(I(\bar x):=\{i:g_i(\bar x)=0\}\), let \(K(\bar x)\) be the critical cone defined in the notation, and let \(\Lambda(\bar x)\) be the KKT multiplier set. If \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer and MFCQ holds at \(\bar x\), then
\[
\max_{(\lambda,\mu)\in\Lambda(\bar x)}d^{\mathsf T}\nabla_{xx}^{2}L(\bar x,\lambda,\mu)d\ge0
\]
for every \(d\in K(\bar x)\). Thus each critical direction admits at least one KKT multiplier, possibly depending on that direction, with nonnegative Lagrangian curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a local minimizer satisfying MFCQ, every critical direction has an admissible KKT multiplier, possibly depending on the direction, for which the Lagrangian has nonnegative second-order curvature.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximized-Hessian second-order sufficient condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition in the generalized-Lagrangian framework; the subsequent pointwise condition is explicitly weaker, not equivalent in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a feasible point \(x_0\in\Phi\), the second-order sufficient condition holds when there exist \(\eta>0\) and \(\beta>0\) such that
\[
\sup_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda_N^g(x_0)}D_{xx}^2L^g(x_0,\alpha,\lambda)(h,h)\ge \beta\lVert h\rVert^2\qquad\forall h\in C_\eta(x_0).
\]
The left-hand side is called the maximized Hessian of the generalized Lagrangian. This condition implies the weaker condition
\[
\forall h\in C(x_0)\setminus\{0\},\ \exists(\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda^g(x_0):\ D_{xx}^2L^g(x_0,\alpha,\lambda)(h,h)>0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The second-order sufficient condition is uniform positive definiteness of the maximized generalized-Lagrangian Hessian on an approximate critical cone. It implies pointwise positive curvature along every nonzero critical direction for a possibly direction-dependent multiplier pair.
assumptions_latex: x_0\in\Phi
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{SOSC}(x_0)\iff\exists\eta,\beta>0\ \forall h\in C_\eta(x_0):\ \sup_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda_N^g(x_0)}D_{xx}^2L^g(x_0,\alpha,\lambda)(h,h)\ge\beta\lVert h\rVert^2;\quad \operatorname{SOSC}(x_0)\Rightarrow(3.137).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic-growth tests for generalized polyhedral constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized-Lagrangian and ordinary-Lagrangian Hessian characterizations on the critical cone when the constraint set is generalized polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\) be generalized polyhedral and let \(x_0\in\Phi\). If there exists \(\beta>0\) such that
\[
\sup_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda_N^g(x_0)}D_{xx}^2L^g(x_0,\alpha,\lambda)(h,h)\ge\beta\lVert h\rVert^2\qquad\forall h\in C(x_0),
\]
then quadratic growth holds at \(x_0\). If, additionally, Robinson's constraint qualification holds at \(x_0\), then quadratic growth holds at \(x_0\) if and only if there exists \(\beta>0\) such that
\[
\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda(x_0)}D_{xx}^2L(x_0,\lambda)(h,h)\ge\beta\lVert h\rVert^2\qquad\forall h\in C(x_0).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For generalized polyhedral constraints, uniform positivity of the maximized generalized-Lagrangian Hessian on the critical cone is sufficient for quadratic growth. Under Robinson's constraint qualification, quadratic growth is equivalent to the corresponding ordinary-Lagrangian multiplier test.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses conditions (3.136) and (3.137) as defined in the surrounding generalized-Lagrangian framework.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

holds, then the second-order growth condition holds at \(x_0\). If \(X\) is finite dimensional, this condition is equivalent to

\]

d^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2f(\bar x)d>0\qquad\text{for every }d\ne0,

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \((\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)\) satisfies the KKT conditions and LICQ holds. If
\[
d^{\mathsf T}\nabla_{xx}^{2}L(\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)d>0
\qquad\text{for all }d\in K(\bar x)\setminus\{0\},
\]
then there exist \(c,r>0\) such that every feasible \(x\) with \(\lVert x-\bar x\rVert<r\) satisfies
\[
f(x)\ge f(\bar x)+\frac c2\lVert x-\bar x\rVert^2.
\]
Consequently, \(\bar x\) is a strict, isolated local minimizer.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(\nabla f(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}d\ge0\) for all \(d\in T_\Omega(\bar x)\), and assume that some \(\alpha>0\) satisfies
\[
\inf_{w\in T^2_\Omega(\bar x;d)}
\left(\nabla f(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}w+d^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2f(\bar x)d\right)
\ge\alpha
\]
for every \(d\in K_f(\bar x)\) with \(\lVert d\rVert=1\). Under parabolic derivability and the regularity ensuring realization of these second-order tangents, there exist \(c,r>0\) such that
\[
f(x)\ge f(\bar x)+\frac c2\lVert x-\bar x\rVert^2
\]
for all \(x\in\Omega\cap B_r(\bar x)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient condition for local quadratic growth in semilinear parabolic boundary control, localized in the control's $L^\infty$ norm and measured quadratically in its $L^2$ norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose Assumption 5.6 holds, and let $(\bar y,\bar u)$ be feasible for the optimal boundary-control problem and satisfy the first-order necessary optimality conditions. If there exist $\delta>0$ and $\tau>0$ such that the definiteness condition (5.49) holds, then there exist $\varepsilon>0$ and $\sigma>0$ such that, for every $u\in U_{ad}$ with associated state $y$ and
\[
\|u-\bar u\|_{L^\infty(\Sigma)}\leq\varepsilon,
\]
one has
\[
J(y,u)\geq J(\bar y,\bar u)+\sigma\|u-\bar u\|_{L^2(\Sigma)}^2.
\]
Consequently, $\bar u$ is locally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assume the referenced regularity hypothesis, feasibility, the first-order necessary conditions, and the stated second-order definiteness condition for some positive delta and tau. Then every admissible control sufficiently close to the reference control in the L-infinity norm satisfies a positive L2 quadratic-growth bound. Thus the reference control is locally optimal in the indicated L-infinity neighborhood.

\[

\qquad\text{for all }x\in B_r(x_p).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform quadratic growth around every nearby stationary point of a parameterized constrained problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let x_0 be stationary for the reference problem. Uniform second-order growth at x_0 relative to a C^2-smooth parameterization (f(x,u),G(x,u)) means that there exist c>0 and neighborhoods \mathcal V_X of x_0 and \mathcal V_U of u_0 such that, for every u\in\mathcal V_U and every stationary point \bar x(u)\in\mathcal V_X of P_u, f(x,u)\geq f(\bar x(u),u)+c\|x-\bar x(u)\|^2 for all x\in\mathcal V_X satisfying G(x,u)\in K. The unqualified uniform second-order growth condition holds when this property holds for every C^2-smooth parameterization. For the canonical parameterization, the condition becomes f(x)-\langle\delta_1,x-\bar x\rangle\geq f(\bar x)+c\|x-\bar x\|^2 for every x\in\mathcal V_X\cap G^{-1}(K-\delta_2).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform second-order growth requires a positive quadratic-growth constant that applies uniformly to nearby parameters, nearby stationary points, and nearby feasible points. Without qualification, the requirement is imposed for every twice-smooth parameterization.
assumptions_latex: x_0\text{ is stationary for the reference problem}
(f(x,u),G(x,u))\text{ is a }C^2\text{-smooth parameterization}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists c>0,\mathcal V_X,\mathcal V_U:\ \forall u\in\mathcal V_U,\ \forall\bar x(u)\in\mathcal V_X\text{ stationary},\ \forall x\in\mathcal V_X\text{ with }G(x,u)\in K,\quad f(x,u)\geq f(\bar x(u),u)+c\|x-\bar x(u)\|^2.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and finite at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\) is a strong local minimizer exactly when it satisfies a local quadratic-growth inequality with positive modulus.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong local minimality in the quadratic-growth sense used in second-order variational analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A point \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}F\) is a strong local minimizer of \(F\) if there exist \(c>0\) and \(r>0\) such that
\[
F(x)\ge F(\bar x)+\frac c2\lVert x-\bar x\rVert^2
\qquad\text{for every }x\in B_r(\bar x).
\]
This inequality implies that \(\bar x\) is the unique minimizer of \(F\) in a possibly smaller neighborhood. Thus strong local minimality is stronger than strict local minimality without a prescribed growth rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strong local minimizer is supported by a positive quadratic lower bound and is therefore locally isolated.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong Local Minimizers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quadratic-growth definition of a strong local minimizer is standard in second-order variational analysis and fits the leaf, but terminology varies across sources. No inspectable citation is provided to establish the intended convention.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is prox-regular and subdifferentially continuous at \((\bar x,0)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional prox-regular, subdifferentially continuous, twice epi-differentiable objectives at a stationary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the stated regularity, the following are equivalent: there exist \(c,r>0\) such that
\[
F(x)\ge F(\bar x)+\frac c2\lVert x-\bar x\rVert^2
\quad\text{for }x\in B_r(\bar x),
\]
and there exists \(\alpha>0\) such that
\[
d_e^2F(\bar x\mid0)(d)\ge\alpha\lVert d\rVert^2
\quad\text{for every }d\in\mathbb R^n.
\]
Thus, within this regularity regime, strong local minimality is characterized by uniform positive second-order epi-curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For regular twice epi-differentiable objectives, local quadratic growth is equivalent to uniformly positive second-order epi-curvature in every direction.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\le0\) and \(h_j(x)=0\). If \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer and LICQ holds, then its KKT multiplier satisfies
\[
d^{\mathsf T}\nabla_{xx}^{2}L(\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)d\ge0
\quad\text{for every }d\in K(\bar x).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(G(x)\in K\). Let \(\lambda\in N_K(G(\bar x))\) satisfy \(\nabla f(\bar x)+G'(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}\lambda=0\). Under a valid second-order chain rule, local minimality requires
\[
d^{\mathsf T}\nabla_{xx}^{2}L(\bar x,\lambda)d
+d^2\delta_K(G(\bar x)\mid\lambda)(G'(\bar x)d)\ge0
\]
for critical directions \(d\in\mathcal C(\bar x,\lambda)\). A uniform strict lower bound by \(\alpha\lVert d\rVert^2\) for all nonzero critical directions is sufficient for quadratic growth. The indicator term records nonpolyhedral cone curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conic second-order tests add the cone indicator's second subderivative to Lagrangian curvature; strict positivity gives quadratic growth under chain-rule regularity.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Map Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean normal-map reformulation of a convex-set variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(P_C\) be its Euclidean projector, and define \[F_C(z)=F(P_Cz)+z-P_Cz.\] The zeros of the normal map and the solutions of the variational inequality correspond by \[F_C(z)=0,\quad x=P_Cz\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad 0\in F(x)+N_C(x),\quad z=x-F(x).\] Consequently, \[\{x\in\mathbb R^n:0\in F(x)+N_C(x)\}=\{P_Cz:z\in\mathbb R^n,\ F_C(z)=0\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The zeros of the normal map correspond exactly to variational-inequality solutions: a zero z gives x=P_Cz, while a solution x gives z=x−F(x).
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is continuous.
\(P_C\) denotes the Euclidean projector onto \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_C(z)=0\) with \(x=P_Cz\) if and only if \(0\in F(x)+N_C(x)\) with \(z=x-F(x)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be prox-regular and subdifferentially continuous at \((\bar x,0)\), where \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer and \(0\in\partial f(\bar x)\). children.title: Isolated-Calmness Criteria
children.top_down_role: Second-order tests for isolated solution behavior under perturbation.

knowledge_statements.title: Isolated-Calmness Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graphical-derivative test for isolated calmness of a subgradient solution map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=(\partial f)^{-1}\), and suppose that \(\operatorname{gph}\partial f\) is locally closed at \((\bar x,\bar v)\). The map \(S\) is isolated calm at \((\bar v,\bar x)\) if and only if \[0\in D(\partial f)(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad w=0.\] Equivalently, \[DS(\bar v\mid\bar x)(0)=\{0\}.\] Isolated calmness means that there are neighborhoods \(V\) of \(\bar v\) and \(U\) of \(\bar x\), and \(\kappa>0\), such that \[S(v)\cap U\subset \bar x+\kappa\|v-\bar v\|\mathbb B\quad\text{for every }v\in V.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the subgradient graph is locally closed, its inverse is isolated calm exactly when the homogeneous graphical linearization has no nonzero primal solution direction.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
\((\bar x,\bar v)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f\).
\(\operatorname{gph}\partial f\) is locally closed at \((\bar x,\bar v)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\partial f)^{-1}\) is isolated calm at \((\bar v,\bar x)\) if and only if \(0\in D(\partial f)(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)\Rightarrow w=0\).

notation.meaning: Graphical derivative of the subgradient mapping

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=(\partial f)^{-1}\). The Aubin property of \(S\) at \((\bar v,\bar x)\) means that some neighborhoods and \(\kappa>0\) satisfy \[S(v_1)\cap U\subset S(v_2)+\kappa\|v_1-v_2\|\mathbb B\] for all nearby \(v_1,v_2\). knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\le0\). Let \((\bar x,\bar\lambda)\) satisfy the KKT conditions and LICQ, and let \(K(\bar x,\bar\lambda)\) be the corresponding critical cone. If there exists \(c>0\) such that \[\langle w,\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar\lambda)w\rangle\ge c\|w\|^2\quad\text{for every }w\in K(\bar x,\bar\lambda),\] then \(\bar x\) is a tilt-stable local minimizer of the constrained problem. The localized minimizer under small linear objective perturbations is therefore unique and Lipschitz continuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under LICQ, uniform positive curvature of the Lagrangian on the critical cone guarantees tilt stability and Lipschitz dependence of the local constrained minimizer.

knowledge_statements.title: Unconstrained Full Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lipschitz full stability under simultaneous tilt and finite-dimensional parameter perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb{R}^n\), \(P=\mathbb{R}^s\), and \(f:X\times P\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\). For \(\gamma>0\), define \[M_\gamma(v,p):=\mathop{\rm argmin}_{x\in B_\gamma(\bar x)}\{f(x,p)-\langle v,x\rangle\},\qquad m_\gamma(v,p):=\inf_{x\in B_\gamma(\bar x)}\{f(x,p)-\langle v,x\rangle\}.\] The minimizer \(\bar x\) is fully stable at \((\bar v,\bar p)\) if some \(\gamma>0\) and neighborhoods of \(\bar v\) and \(\bar p\) make \(M_\gamma\) single-valued and Lipschitz, with \(M_\gamma(\bar v,\bar p)=\bar x\), and make \(m_\gamma\) Lipschitz on the same product neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local minimizer is fully stable when small finite-dimensional tilt and parameter changes produce a unique nearby minimizer and locally Lipschitz minimizer and value mappings.
assumptions_latex: \(X=\mathbb{R}^n\), \(P=\mathbb{R}^s\), and \(f:X\times P\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is proper and lower semicontinuous near \((\bar x,\bar p)\).
\(\bar x\) locally minimizes \(f(\cdot,\bar p)-\langle\bar v,\cdot\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The localized minimizer and value mappings are single-valued Lipschitz near \((\bar v,\bar p)\).

children.title: Full Stability in Nonlinear Programming
children.top_down_role: Multiplier-sensitive full stability for smooth constraint systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Full Stability in Nonlinear Programming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear programs with equality and inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(p\in\mathbb{R}^s\), \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^s\to\mathbb{R}^q\), and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^s\to\mathbb{R}^m\). Consider minimizing \(\varphi(x,p)-\langle v,x\rangle\) subject to \(h(x,p)=0\) and \(g(x,p)\leq0\). Suppose \((\bar x,\bar p)\) is feasible and stationary at tilt \(\bar v\), LICQ holds there, and \(\bar\lambda\) is the resulting unique KKT multiplier. Let \(K(\bar x,\bar p,\bar\lambda)\) be the associated critical cone. If \[\langle d,\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar p,\bar\lambda)d\rangle>0\quad\text{for every }d\in K(\bar x,\bar p,\bar\lambda)\setminus\{0\},\] then the localized primal-multiplier KKT solution mapping in \((v,p)\) is single-valued and Lipschitz. Consequently, \(\bar x\) is a fully stable local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear program, LICQ and positive Lagrangian curvature on every nonzero critical direction yield a locally unique Lipschitz primal-multiplier solution and full stability.
assumptions_latex: \(\varphi\), \(h\), and \(g\) are \(C^2\) near \((\bar x,\bar p)\), with \(h\) equality-valued in \(\mathbb{R}^q\) and \(g\) inequality-valued in \(\mathbb{R}^m\).
\((\bar x,\bar p)\) is a feasible KKT point at tilt \(\bar v\).
LICQ holds at \((\bar x,\bar p)\), giving the unique multiplier \(\bar\lambda\).
The strong second-order sufficient condition holds on the critical cone \(K(\bar x,\bar p,\bar\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The localized primal-multiplier solution is single-valued Lipschitz, and \(\bar x\) is a fully stable local minimizer.

notation.meaning: critical cone at the reference KKT point

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform second-order coercivity near a perturbation direction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Promotes pointwise positivity of Legendre Lagrangian Hessians to a uniform quadratic lower bound over nearby directional dual solution sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose X is a reflexive Banach space, x_0\in X, \Lambda(x_0,u_0)\ne\varnothing, and directional regularity holds at x_0 in direction d. Assume h\mapsto D_{xx}^2G(x_0,u_0)(h,h) is continuous from the weak topology of X to the strong topology of Y. For every \lambda\in\mathcal S(DL_d), assume D_{xx}^2L(x_0,\lambda,u_0) is a Legendre form and D_{xx}^2L(x_0,\lambda,u_0)(h,h)>0 for every h\in C(x_0)\setminus\{0\}. Then there exists \beta>0 such that, for every d' sufficiently close to d, \inf_{\lambda\in\mathcal S(DL_{d'})}D_{xx}^2L(x_0,\lambda,u_0)(h,h)\ge\beta\|h\|^2 for every h\in C.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a reflexive Banach space, weak-to-strong continuity of constraint curvature, Legendre-form Lagrangian Hessians, and pointwise positivity on nonzero critical directions imply uniform quadratic coercivity over directional dual solutions for all nearby perturbation directions.
assumptions_latex: X\text{ is a reflexive Banach space}
x_0\in X
\Lambda(x_0,u_0)\ne\varnothing
\text{Directional regularity holds at }x_0\text{ in direction }d
h\mapsto D_{xx}^2G(x_0,u_0)(h,h)\text{ is weak-to-strong continuous from }X\text{ to }Y
D_{xx}^2L(x_0,\lambda,u_0)\text{ is a Legendre form for every }\lambda\in\mathcal S(DL_d)
D_{xx}^2L(x_0,\lambda,u_0)(h,h)>0\quad\forall\lambda\in\mathcal S(DL_d),\ \forall h\in C(x_0)\setminus\{0\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\beta>0\ \forall d'\text{ sufficiently close to }d:\ \inf_{\lambda\in\mathcal S(DL_{d'})}D_{xx}^2L(x_0,\lambda,u_0)(h,h)\ge\beta\|h\|^2\quad\forall h\in C

children.title: Generalized-Equation Full Stability
children.top_down_role: Full-stability criteria for parameterized generalized equations.

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized-Equation Full Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lipschitz full stability for finite-dimensional parameterized generalized equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb{R}^n\), \(P=\mathbb{R}^s\), and \(F:X\times P\rightrightarrows X\). Define \[S(v,p):=\{x\in X\mid 0\in F(x,p)+v\}.\] The reference solution \(\bar x\) is fully stable at \((\bar v,\bar p)\) if neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(W\) of \((\bar v,\bar p)\) exist such that \(S_U(v,p):=S(v,p)\cap U\) is a singleton for every \((v,p)\in W\), \(S_U(\bar v,\bar p)=\{\bar x\}\), and the resulting selection is Lipschitz on \(W\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-dimensional generalized-equation solution is fully stable when every nearby perturbation has one nearby solution and that solution varies Lipschitz-continuously.
assumptions_latex: \(X=\mathbb{R}^n\), \(P=\mathbb{R}^s\), and \(F:X\times P\rightrightarrows X\) has locally closed graph near \(((\bar x,\bar p),-\bar v)\).
\(0\in F(\bar x,\bar p)+\bar v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Full stability means that the perturbed generalized equation has a unique nearby solution depending Lipschitz-continuously on \((v,p)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Variational-Inequality Full Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional variational inequalities over parameterized closed convex sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\mathbb{R}^s\), let \(C(p)\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed and convex, and let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\times P\to\mathbb{R}^n\). The perturbed variational inequality is \[\langle F(x,p)+v,y-x\rangle\geq0\quad\text{for every }y\in C(p),\] equivalently \(0\in F(x,p)+v+N_{C(p)}(x)\). Define \(S(v,p)\) as its solution set. The reference solution \(\bar x\) is fully stable at \((\bar v,\bar p)\) if some neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) makes \(S(v,p)\cap U\) a singleton for every nearby \((v,p)\), and the resulting local solution selection is Lipschitz in \((v,p)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full stability of this variational inequality is local uniqueness and Lipschitz dependence of its nearby solution on the tilt and model parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(P=\mathbb{R}^s\), and \(C(p)\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is closed and convex for \(p\) near \(\bar p\).
\(F:\mathbb{R}^n\times P\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is continuous near \((\bar x,\bar p)\).
\(\bar x\in C(\bar p)\) solves the reference variational inequality at tilt \(\bar v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Full stability is the single-valued Lipschitz localization of the variational-inequality solution mapping.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a parameter direction \(q\), every graphical derivative \(w\in DS(\bar p,\bar x)(q)\) satisfies the linearized generalized equation \[0\in DM(\bar x,\bar p,0)(w,q).\] Under proto-differentiability and the regularity ensuring exact graphical linearization, the converse also holds, so \[DS(\bar p,\bar x)(q)=\{w\in X\mid0\in DM(\bar x,\bar p,0)(w,q)\}.\] If the right-hand side is a singleton for every \(q\), it gives the directional derivative of the localized solution selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The directional derivative of a solution mapping is obtained by solving the generalized equation formed from the graphical derivative of the original system.

knowledge_statements.title: Criticality Transition Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth fixed-active-set boundary between critical and noncritical multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the columns of \(Z\) form a basis for the tangent space determined by the active constraints, and set \(H_R:=Z^*\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar\lambda)Z\). Within a regime having a fixed active manifold, LICQ, and strict complementarity, the multiplier is noncritical exactly when \(H_R\) is nonsingular. Hence the criticality boundary within this regime is \[\det H_R=0,\] equivalently \(0\in\operatorname{spec}(H_R)\). At a boundary point, a nonzero tangent direction solves the homogeneous linearized KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a fixed regular active set and strict complementarity, the boundary between critical and noncritical multipliers is where the reduced Lagrangian Hessian has a zero eigenvalue.
assumptions_latex: The active constraint manifold is fixed locally and satisfies LICQ.
Strict complementarity holds, so the critical tangent subspace is locally constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Within the stated regime, criticality occurs exactly when the reduced Hessian \(H_R\) is singular.

source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) is variationally convex at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\) if there exist neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(V\) of \(\bar v\), a number \(\varepsilon>0\), and a proper closed convex function \(\widehat f\) such that \[(U\times V)\cap\operatorname{gph}\partial f\cap\{(x,v):f(x)<f(\bar x)+\varepsilon\}=(U\times V)\cap\operatorname{gph}\partial\widehat f\cap\{(x,v):\widehat f(x)<f(\bar x)+\varepsilon\},\] and \(f(x)=\widehat f(x)\) at every pair in this common localized graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function is variationally convex when its nearby low-level subgradient graph and values coincide with those of a closed convex function.

notation.meaning: Limiting subdifferential of the extended-real function.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) is strongly variationally convex at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\) with modulus \(\sigma>0\) if there exist neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(V\) of \(\bar v\), and a proper lower-semicontinuous \(\sigma\)-strongly convex function \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\), such that \(g\leq f\) on \(U\), \[\operatorname{gph}\partial f\cap(U\times V)=\operatorname{gph}\partial g\cap(U\times V),\] and \(f(x)=g(x)\) whenever \((x,v)\) belongs to this common localized graph.

children.title: Second-Subderivative Characterizations
children.top_down_role: Primal second-order tests for variational convexity.

assumptions_latex: The function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is prox-regular and subdifferentially continuous near \((\bar x,\bar v)\).
At every nearby graph point, \(f\) is properly twice epi-differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Localized variational convexity is equivalent to nonnegativity of all nearby second subderivatives; modulus \(\sigma\) corresponds to the lower bound \(\sigma\|w\|^2\).

notation.meaning: Second subderivative of the function at a subgradient pair.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal criterion using the second-subderivative normalization with denominator one-half squared step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Using \[d^2f(x\mid v)(w):=\liminf_{\substack{t\downarrow0\\w'\to w}}\frac{f(x+tw')-f(x)-t\langle v,w'\rangle}{\tfrac12t^2},\] the function \(f\) is variationally convex at \((\bar x,\bar v)\) exactly when neighborhoods \(U,V\) exist such that \(d^2f(x\mid v)(w)\geq0\) for every \((x,v)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f\cap(U\times V)\) and every \(w\). Its strong form with modulus \(\sigma>0\) is characterized by \(d^2f(x\mid v)(w)\geq\sigma\|w\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nearby second subderivatives are nonnegative precisely in the variationally convex regime, and a uniform quadratic lower bound gives strong variational convexity.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) is variationally convex at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\) exactly when neighborhoods \(U,V\) can be chosen so that, for all \((x_i,v_i)\in G\), \[\langle v_1-v_2,x_1-x_2\rangle\geq0.\] It is strongly variationally convex with modulus \(\sigma>0\) exactly when the localized inequality can be strengthened to \[\langle v_1-v_2,x_1-x_2\rangle\geq\sigma\|x_1-x_2\|^2.\]

children.title: Unconstrained Variational Sufficiency
children.top_down_role: Variational sufficiency for extended-real unconstrained models.

assumptions_latex: The function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is proper and lower semicontinuous, with \(0\in\partial f(\bar x)\).
The function is variationally convex at \(\bar x\) for \(0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The point \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer; under modulus \(\sigma>0\), \(f(x)\geq f(\bar x)+\tfrac{\sigma}{2}\|x-\bar x\|^2\) locally.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained extended-real minimization with limiting stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Variational convexity at the stationary pair \((\bar x,0)\) implies that a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) exists such that \[f(x)\geq f(\bar x)\quad\text{for all }x\in U.\] If the variational convexity is strong with modulus \(\sigma>0\), then, after possibly shrinking \(U\), \[f(x)\geq f(\bar x)+\frac{\sigma}{2}\|x-\bar x\|^2\quad\text{for all }x\in U.\] Thus stationarity becomes a local, respectively strong local, sufficiency certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a variationally convex stationary point, first-order stationarity is sufficient for local optimality; the strong regime supplies quadratic growth.
knowledge_statements.title: Unconstrained Variational Sufficiency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sufficiency conclusion is plausible under the intended localized-model definition, but its validity depends on the exact variational-convexity localization, for which no source is supplied.

The point \(\bar x\in C\) satisfies \(0\in\partial F(\bar x)\).
The extended objective \(F\) is variationally convex at \((\bar x,0)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The point \(\bar x\) locally minimizes \(\varphi\) over \(C\), with quadratic growth when \(F\) is strongly variationally convex.

notation.meaning: Indicator function of the feasible set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint systems represented by an indicator-augmented objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There is a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) such that \[\varphi(x)\geq\varphi(\bar x)\quad\text{for every }x\in C\cap U.\] If \(F\) is strongly variationally convex at \((\bar x,0)\) with modulus \(\sigma>0\), then \(U\) may be chosen so that \[\varphi(x)\geq\varphi(\bar x)+\frac{\sigma}{2}\|x-\bar x\|^2\quad\text{for every }x\in C\cap U.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply variational sufficiency to the objective plus the feasible-set indicator; strong variational convexity yields constrained quadratic growth.
knowledge_statements.title: Constrained Variational Sufficiency

children.title: Sufficiency-Transfer Failure
children.top_down_role: Boundaries where variational sufficiency does not transfer to tilt stability.

knowledge_statements.title: Sufficiency-Transfer Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit smooth convex example separating strict sufficiency from tilt stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The point \(0\) is the unique global minimizer of \(f(x)=x^4\), and \(f\) is convex with \(f'(0)=0\). Nevertheless, no constants \(c>0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) satisfy \(x^4\geq c x^2\) for every \(|x|<\varepsilon\). Moreover, the tilted problem has the unique solution \[M(v)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\{x^4-vx\}=\sqrt[3]{v/4},\] which is not Lipschitz at \(v=0\). Thus ordinary convex sufficiency and strict minimality do not transfer to strong variational sufficiency or tilt stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimizer of the convex function x⁴ is strict but lacks quadratic growth; its tilted minimizer varies by a cube root and is not Lipschitz.
assumptions_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\) be defined by \(f(x)=x^4\), with reference point \(\bar x=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strict minimality and ordinary variational sufficiency do not imply quadratic growth or tilt stability.

assumptions_latex: The function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is proper and lower semicontinuous, and the goal is to solve \(0\in\partial f(x)\).
At each accepted iterate, the displayed coderivative inclusion is solvable.

source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I
Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), at iteration \(k\) choose \(v_k\in\partial f(x_k)\). If \(\|v_k\|\leq\varepsilon\), stop and output \(x_k\). Otherwise find a direction \(d_k\) satisfying the coderivative Newton inclusion \[-v_k\in\partial^2f(x_k,v_k)(d_k),\] set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\), and repeat. A globalization may replace the full step by \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\) with \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select a subgradient, invert the coderivative generalized Hessian against it, update the iterate, and stop when the selected subgradient is small.

children.title: Second-Order Bundle Models
children.top_down_role: Generalized-curvature models used within nonsmooth bundle frameworks.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is locally Lipschitz.
A bundle contains sampled triples \((x_i,f_i,g_i)\) with \(f_i=f(x_i)\) and \(g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_k\) is a computable piecewise-quadratic lower model whenever every sampled quadratic is a local lower support for \(f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite maximum of sampled quadratic support models for a nonsmooth objective.

source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(i\in I_k\), define the sampled quadratic \[q_i(x)=f_i+\langle g_i,x-x_i\rangle+\tfrac12\langle x-x_i,H_i(x-x_i)\rangle.\] The second-order bundle model is the representation \[m_k(x)=\max_{i\in I_k}q_i(x).\] If \(q_i(x)\leq f(x)\) on a common neighborhood for every \(i\in I_k\), then \(m_k(x)\leq f(x)\) there. With \(H_i=0\), this construction reduces to the ordinary cutting-plane bundle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A second-order bundle model is the maximum of sampled quadratic supports, reducing to a cutting-plane model when all curvature matrices vanish.

children.title: Second-Order Proximal Models
children.top_down_role: Generalized-curvature models used within proximal local-approximation frameworks.

assumptions_latex: \(m_k:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The proximal parameter satisfies \(t_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model has a unique proximal trial point \(y_k\), characterized by \(0\in\partial m_k(y_k)+t_k^{-1}(y_k-x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex proximal regularization of a local second-order or bundle model.

source_refs.source_title: The Linear Complementarity Problem

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The second-order proximal model centered at \(x_k\) is \[M_k(y;x_k)=m_k(y)+\frac{1}{2t_k}\lVert y-x_k\rVert^2.\] Its trial point is \[y_k=\mathop{\arg\min}_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}M_k(y;x_k).\] Strong convexity of \(M_k(\cdot;x_k)\) makes \(y_k\) unique, and optimality is equivalent to \[0\in\partial m_k(y_k)+t_k^{-1}(y_k-x_k).\] Thus the proximal term both stabilizes the possibly nonsmooth local model and supplies a directly computable stationarity residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add a positive quadratic proximal term to a convex local model; the resulting strongly convex problem has a unique, verifiably stationary trial point.
knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Proximal Models

children.title: Hybrid Bundle–Proximal Regimes
children.top_down_role: Computational regimes combining bundle information with proximal stabilization.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is locally Lipschitz and bounded below on the relevant level set.
At iteration \(k\), \(m_k\) is a proper closed convex bundle model and \(t_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration either moves the prox-center or enriches the model while retaining the center.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic serious-step/null-step bundle–proximal regime; no specific convergence theorem is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a prox-center \(x_0\), bundle model \(m_0\), parameters \(t_k>0\), and \(\eta\in(0,1)\). Compute \[y_k=\mathop{\arg\min}_y\left\{m_k(y)+\frac{1}{2t_k}\lVert y-x_k\rVert^2\right\},\qquad \Delta_k=f(x_k)-m_k(y_k).\] If \(\Delta_k\leq\varepsilon\), return \(x_k\). Otherwise evaluate \(f(y_k)\) and a subgradient at \(y_k\). If \(f(x_k)-f(y_k)\geq\eta\Delta_k\), take a serious step \(x_{k+1}=y_k\); otherwise take a null step \(x_{k+1}=x_k\). In both cases, augment the bundle with the new information and construct \(m_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stabilized bundle trial is accepted as a serious step when actual decrease matches predicted decrease; otherwise it only enriches the model.
knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Bundle–Proximal Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The serious-step/null-step scheme fits the algorithmic leaf, but the acceptance ratio, predicted decrease, stopping rule, and bundle update regime require a direct source.

knowledge_statements.title: Critical-Cone Curvature Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional nonlinear-programming certificate on the multiplier-dependent critical cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A critical-cone curvature certificate is a scalar \(\mu>0\) satisfying \[d^{\mathsf T}Hd\geq\mu\lVert d\rVert^2\qquad\text{for every }d\in K(\bar x,\bar\lambda).\] If \(K(\bar x,\bar\lambda)\) contains a nonzero direction, homogeneity gives the equivalent normalized condition \[\inf\left\{d^{\mathsf T}Hd:d\in K(\bar x,\bar\lambda),\ \lVert d\rVert=1\right\}\geq\mu.\] The certificate records positive Lagrangian curvature along the critical directions relevant to constrained optimality rather than requiring positive definiteness on the whole ambient space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive lower bound for Lagrangian curvature on all critical directions certifies second-order positivity on the geometry relevant to constrained optimality; normalization to unit directions applies when such directions exist.
assumptions_latex: \((\bar x,\bar\lambda)\) satisfies the KKT conditions for a twice continuously differentiable nonlinear program.
A constraint qualification identifies the critical cone \(K(\bar x,\bar\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strict positivity of the Lagrangian Hessian on every nonzero critical direction is a verifiable second-order curvature certificate.

The bound implies that every \(V\in\partial F(\bar x)\) is invertible and \(\lVert V^{-1}\rVert\leq\gamma^{-1}\). Upper semicontinuity of \(\partial F\) then preserves a positive nonsingularity margin in a sufficiently small neighborhood of \(\bar x\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A stability certificate for \(T\) at \((\bar x,\bar v)\) consists of neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar x\), \(V\) of \(\bar v\), a mapping \(s:V\to U\), and \(\kappa\geq0\) such that \[T^{-1}(v)\cap U=\{s(v)\}\quad\text{for every }v\in V,\] and \[\lVert s(v_1)-s(v_2)\rVert\leq\kappa\lVert v_1-v_2\rVert\quad\text{for all }v_1,v_2\in V.\] These finite local data certify uniqueness and Lipschitz stability of the solution selected near \(\bar x\) under perturbations near \(\bar v\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A quadratic-growth certificate at \(\bar x\) is a pair \((\mu,r)\) with \(\mu>0\) and \(r>0\) for which \[f(x)\geq f(\bar x)+\frac{\mu}{2}\lVert x-\bar x\rVert^2\qquad\text{whenever }\lVert x-\bar x\rVert\leq r.\] The inequality directly certifies that \(\bar x\) is a strict local minimizer and quantitatively separates objective values from \(f(\bar x)\). assumptions_latex: \(x_k\to \bar x\) in a normed space.
\(x_k\ne \bar x\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).

source_refs.source_title: The Linear Complementarity Problem

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A sequence \((x_k)\) converging to \(\bar x\) is locally Q-linearly convergent if there exist \(q\in[0,1)\) and \(k_0\) such that
\[
\|x_{k+1}-\bar x\|\le q\|x_k-\bar x\|\qquad(k\ge k_0).
\]
Equivalently, when the error is eventually nonzero, its asymptotic quotient satisfies
\[
\limsup_{k\to\infty}\frac{\|x_{k+1}-\bar x\|}{\|x_k-\bar x\|}<1.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local Q-linear convergence means that, near the limit, each iterate’s error is bounded by a fixed contraction factor smaller than one times the preceding error.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Local Convergence

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A sequence \((x_k)\) converging to \(\bar x\) is locally Q-superlinearly convergent if
\[
\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{\|x_{k+1}-\bar x\|}{\|x_k-\bar x\|}=0.
\]
Thus the next error satisfies \(\|x_{k+1}-\bar x\|=o(\|x_k-\bar x\|)\). This rate is strictly stronger than Q-linear convergence whenever the sequence does not reach \(\bar x\) finitely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local Q-superlinear convergence means that the ratio of successive errors tends to zero, so no fixed positive contraction factor describes the asymptotic rate.

\|x_{k+1}-\bar x\|\le C\|x_k-\bar x\|^2\qquad(k\ge k_0).
\]
If the sequence does not terminate finitely, this estimate implies Q-superlinear convergence because \(C\|x_k-\bar x\|\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local Q-quadratic convergence means that the next error is eventually bounded by a constant times the square of the current error.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Local Convergence

children.title: Second-Order Object Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Failures of existence, convergence, or identification of second-order objects.

children.title: Failure of Twice Epi-Differentiability
children.top_down_role: Nonexistence or instability of second epigraphical limits.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
\(f(\bar x)\) is finite and \(\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{e-liminf}_{t\downarrow0}\Delta_t^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)\ne\operatorname*{e-limsup}_{t\downarrow0}\Delta_t^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure is expressed by unequal lower and upper epigraphical limits.

source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis
Modern Nonconvex Nondifferentiable Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(t>0\), define
\[
\Delta_t^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w):=\frac{f(\bar x+tw)-f(\bar x)-t\langle\bar v,w\rangle}{\tfrac12t^2}.
\]
Twice epi-differentiability of \(f\) at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\) fails precisely when this family has no epigraphical limit as \(t\downarrow0\), equivalently when
\[
\operatorname*{e-liminf}_{t\downarrow0}\Delta_t^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)
\ne
\operatorname*{e-limsup}_{t\downarrow0}\Delta_t^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Twice epi-differentiability fails when the second-order difference quotients have different lower and upper epigraphical limits as the scale tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure of Twice Epi-Differentiability
